# graphics.library V40 inventory audit

This is the zero-hole manifest audit for the Kickstart 3.1/V40 replacement.
It is deliberately separate from the semantic-conformance ledger: a vector can
have a register adapter case while still being intentionally delegated to a
CopperStart/native display boundary, layers.library, or the separate CyberGraphX
patch.

The independently selectable implementation units are catalogued in
[`GRAPHICS_LIBRARY_REPLACEMENT_GOALS.md`](GRAPHICS_LIBRARY_REPLACEMENT_GOALS.md);
this inventory remains the vector/ownership manifest rather than a progress
ledger.

## Latest native screen/view lifecycle unit

The lifecycle entries are listed in the table below; the latest bounded
drawing unit is recorded separately immediately above it.

## Latest layered raster/damage unit

At execution checkpoint 676, the paused/resumed caller-Region fixture covers
`SetRast`, `ClipBlit`,
`BltBitMapRastPort`, `RectFill`, `BltPattern`, and `EraseRect` with active
damage and independent endpoint scroll transforms. ClipBlit writes only the
source/destination Region and damage intersection; bitmap blit and RectFill
write both destination Region pixels, while alternating `0xAAAA` AreaPtrn
patterning writes only `(4,4)` after scroll projection. EraseRect clears both
admitted pixels using BPen, restores APen, and advances line phase to 15. Flags,
caller Region, and Layers-owned damage remain intact. A patterned Move/Draw
segment across the same pixels plots only `(4,4)`, advances the cursor to
`(5,4)`, and advances line phase to 12. Focused coverage passes 1/1, the Layers
suite 101/101, and combined graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079. A real Topaz Text glyph
also projects through the same caller Region and active damage, plotting its
known `(4,4)` sample without changing other pixels and advancing CurrentX from
3 to 11. PolyDraw now carries pattern phase across two vertices and plots only
`(4,4)`, ending at cursor `(4,4)` and phase 13. Focused coverage passes 1/1,
the Layers suite 101/101, and combined graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079. Polygon
`AreaEnd` fills only the two admitted screen pixels `(4,4)` and `(5,4)`.
`WritePixel` changes only `(4,4)`; `ReadPixel` returns 1 there, 0 at the other
admitted pixel, and `uint.MaxValue` for a hidden caller-Region point.
Surface-mode `Flood` traverses the connected source-color region but publishes
only `(4,4)` and `(5,4)`. Layer flags, caller Region, and Layers-owned damage
bytes remain unchanged. Focused coverage passes 1/1, the Layers suite 101/101,
and combined graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079. `DrawEllipse` writes only its
admitted right-hand cardinal sample `(5,4)`; `AreaEllipse` followed by `AreaEnd`
fills only `(4,4)` and `(5,4)`. `ScrollRaster` moves screen `(5,4)` to `(4,4)`
and backfills with BPen; full-displacement `ScrollRasterBF` clears only those
two caller-Region pixels. Seeded `ClearEOL` and `ClearScreen` also clear only
`(4,4)` and `(5,4)`. Layer flags, caller Region, and Layers-owned damage bytes
remain unchanged. Focused coverage passes 1/1, the Layers suite 101/101, and
combined graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079. `BltTemplate` writes only `(4,4)` and
`(5,4)` from five set source bits. `WritePixelLine8` and `WritePixelArray8`
report five samples while publishing only those pixels. `ReadPixelLine8` and
`ReadPixelArray8` return 1,1 for the admitted samples and zero for the hidden
remainder. Layer flags, caller Region, and Layers-owned damage bytes remain
unchanged. Focused coverage passes 1/1, the Layers suite 101/101, and combined
graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079. `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` applies its one-bit mask
inside the caller-Region/damage projection and writes only `(4,4)` although
`(5,4)` is also admitted. Standard-planar `WriteChunkyPixels` keeps its
five-sample request but publishes only `(4,4)` and `(5,4)`. Layer flags, caller
Region, and Layers-owned damage bytes remain unchanged. Focused coverage passes
1/1, the Layers suite 101/101, and combined graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079. Border
`Flood` now stops at an explicit four-pixel `OutlinePen=1` ring around the
projected seed. Complement mode makes an accidental write to the admitted
outline pixel visible; exact raster comparison confirms the ring and filled
seed while preserving caller Region, resumed damage, layer flags, and damage
bytes. Focused coverage passes 1/1, the Layers suite 101/101, and combined
graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079. Border-mode `Flood` also stops at an explicit
four-pixel `OutlinePen=1` ring around the projected seed; complement mode
makes an accidental outline write observable. The exact raster check confirms
the intact ring and filled seed while caller Region, resumed damage, layer
flags, and damage bytes remain unchanged. Focused coverage passes 1/1; Layers
passes 101/101; combined graphics/Layers passes 2,079/2,079.

## Latest native Region boolean unit

  At checkpoint 680, `OrRegionRegion`/`XorRegionRegion` retain strict-gap
insertion for a canonical one-node source between two destination nodes. OR
also admits top and bottom protrusions when the source X span is strictly
inside the first node. Bottom overlap inserts its exposed lower strip between
the destination nodes; top overlap prepends its exposed upper strip and
updates the head/sentinel links. Both forms validate ownership, complete links,
matching envelopes, relative bounds, and exact topology before allocation;
the source is preserved and allocation failure leaves the old chain intact.
OR also handles one source protruding both above and below the first
destination node while remaining strictly X-contained and above the second.
The additional bounded OR arm accepts a source starting inside the first node,
extending beyond its right edge, and occupying a strict interior Y band. Its
portable and native results agree on upper old-width, widened middle, lower
old-width, and unchanged second-node rectangles. It reuses the first node for
the middle and transactionally allocates the upper/lower residuals;
allocation/address-class failures preserve the source and old chain. The
left-edge mirror and bounded two-sided X overhang share the same transaction;
all three horizontal orientations retain old-width upper/lower bands and widen
  only the middle node's contributed X edge(s). The top-overlap mirror now
  covers right-, left-, and both-edge X overhang when the source begins above
  the first node and overlaps its strict interior Y band. Right/left publish
  upper, widened-middle, and lower bands using two nodes; both-edge coalesces
  the equal-width upper/middle bands into one allocation and reuses the first
  node for the lower residual. AccurateM68000 success/failure and portable
  differential fixtures cover all orientations and preserve the source and
  prior chain on allocation failure. The relative-Y bounds proof uses the
  Region Y origin. Bottom overlap now covers right-, left-, and both-edge X
  overhang: right/left publish upper old-width, widened-middle, and lower
  source-width bands with two allocations; both-edge coalesces the middle and
  lower bands with one new node. AccurateM68000 fixtures verify every
  top/bottom and X orientation, exact links/bounds, allocation rollback,
  invalid-address cleanup, and unchanged source/old chain; nine portable
  differentials agree. RegionUnion plus signed-branch audit passes 407/407;
  combined Region/scaffold/Layers regression passes 2,486/2,486. Generated
  image: 1,510,780 bytes / 76,704 branches / 3,428 relays / 7 chains / 3,346
  boundaries. Next: cover a source spanning both vertical edges of the first
  destination node while overhanging one or both horizontal edges, beginning
  with portable canonical bands. Other overlapping union, XOR, and subtraction
  forms remain open. CyberGraphX remains excluded.

## Previous layered raster/damage unit

Simultaneous active damage at both simple-layer endpoints is covered with
different scroll offsets and a patterned source, verifying the exact
screen-space intersection after each logical transform. Focused coverage
passes 1/1, the Layers suite 101/101, and combined graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079.

Active source and destination SuperBitMap layers with valid empty DamageLists
are covered independently. Neither the stable destination nor an active
destination's display, compact backing, or off-viewport SuperBitMap storage
may change. The current Layers topology path does not publish nonempty damage
for `LayerFlags.Super`, so no unreachable nonempty Super update is synthesized.
Focused coverage passes 1/1, the Layers suite 101/101, and combined
graphics/Layers 2,079/2,079.

G289 extends the native V40.63 reachability probe through SuperBitMap creation,
blocker deletion, `ScrollLayer`, `MoveSizeLayer`, `BeginUpdate`, and incomplete
`EndUpdate`. The native and CopperStart traces match and every DamageList
remains empty; no synthetic nonempty SuperBitMap projection is fed to
`ClipBlit`.

Both independent simple-layer ClipBlit endpoints enter `BeginUpdate` with
intentionally different damage partitions. The gateway copies only their
exact intersection; each endpoint has exclusive pixels. Every destination
pixel is checked and layer flags and damage ownership remain unchanged.
Focused coverage passes 1/1, the Layers suite 100/100, and combined
graphics/Layers 2,078/2,078.

The dual-layer graphics.library `ClipBlit` gateway also covers an active
destination update intersected with a restricted source ClipRect, and verifies
the destination temporary damage ClipRects alone bound a full-area transfer.
Source/destination flags and damage ownership remain unchanged. Focused
coverage passes 1/1, the full Layers suite 99/99, and combined graphics/Layers
2,077/2,077.

During active `BeginUpdate`, the validated layer-raster provider uses the
current ClipRect head as the complete damage domain and does not independently
append off-viewport SuperClipRect fragments. A real graphics.library `RectFill`
regression verifies that an empty but valid damage Region leaves display,
compact backing, and SuperBitMap pixels unchanged, without mutating
`Layer.Flags` or the DamageList header. The separate nonempty simple-layer test
verifies exact active damage islands for full-area `RectFill` and
`BltBitMapRastPort` calls through the actual gateway. Focused coverage passes
3/3, the full Layers suite 98/98, and combined graphics/Layers 2,076/2,076.
G290 verifies `ClipBlit` with two disconnected simple-layer damage islands at
both endpoints and caller clipping. Native V40.63 and CopperStart copy exactly
the four pixels shared by the active source and destination projections, while
preserving exclusive pixels and both endpoints' DamageList/ClipRect ownership.

## Authority and evidence

- Manifest authority: `CopperMod.Amiga.Emulator/CopperStart/Graphics/Portable/GraphicsLvo.cs`.
- The manifest contains **163 public vectors**, all negative six-byte-aligned
  offsets from `-30` through `-1056`.
- The reserved V40 gap at `-648` is not a public `GraphicsLvo` entry and is
  retained as an explicit native fallback slot by the ROM image builder.
- A newer V39 autodoc page names `VPOrigin`, but the NDK 3.2R4
  `graphics_lib.fd` keeps both slots between `-636` and `-654` private. Until a
  Kickstart ROM vector-table proof says otherwise, `VPOrigin` remains a future
  extension boundary and is not overlaid ([VPOrigin autodoc](https://developer.amigaos3.net/autodocs/graphics.library/VPOrigin.html);
  [NDK graphics_lib.fd](https://megaburken.net/~patrik/NDK3.2R4/FD/graphics_lib.fd)).
- `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests.V40ManifestContainsAllPublicVectorsAndAlignedOffsets`
  verifies the count, uniqueness, bounds, alignment, reserved `-648` gap, and
  representative ABI offsets.
- `GraphicsLibraryPortableScaffoldTests.NativeGraphicsOverlayManifestContainsOnlyGuestMemorySafeVectors`
  verifies that the reversible ROM overlay admits all public vectors;
  scheduler-sensitive layer-lock entries return the Layers gateway's exact
  completion/block result, while provider-backed blitter, GELS, and
  super-bitmap vectors remain conditional claims and tail-chain when their
  explicit CopperStart/native owner is absent.
- `CopperStartGraphicsRegisterAdapter.TryInvoke` has an explicit switch case
  for every entry below. A `false` result is an intentional provider boundary,
  not an unassigned vector: the caller may chain to the resident ROM or to a
  provider such as layers.library/CyberGraphX.

## Explicit provider boundaries

The following are intentionally not claimed as host-side portable behavior when
the required owner is absent:

- Layered RastPorts: clipping, damage, backing-store, and private `ClipRect`
  state remain with layers.library or its host/native provider.
- RTG/CyberGraphX bitmaps and RastPorts: allocation, blits, attributes,
  viewport replacement, and palette publication fall through without changing
  the guest D-register sentinel.
- Copper/custom-chip/display timing: `MrgCop`, `MakeVPort`, `LoadView`,
  `WaitTOF`, `WaitBOVP`, `CalcIVG`, `SetChipRev`, palette publication, and
  double-buffer message delivery use explicit CopperStart/native callbacks.
- Synthetic screen/view lifecycle: standard-planar and RTG screen bitmap
  construction clears partial plane/RasInfo/BitMap state on late allocation or
  dual-playfield-link failure, so retry and close/reopen paths cannot publish a
  stale half-built surface.
- Synthetic rethink validation: `RethinkDisplay` applies the same exact
  present-chain RasInfo cardinality as `LoadView`/`MrgCop` before allocating
  replacement CPR/raw lists; a readable extra DUALPF node preserves the
  currently loaded stream, while a null assembly head remains legal.
- CloseScreen publication: a mid-frame synthetic close preserves the active
  copper stream until the next PAL/NTSC frame boundary, then publishes the
  blanking list through the same queued `LoadView(NULL)` boundary.
- Alternating-field publication: queued `LofCprList`/`ShfCprList` pairs are
  selected from the canonical PAL/NTSC beam-clock long/short-frame state at
  the publication boundary; a single resolved list remains the fallback for
  assembly and non-interlaced paths.
- DBufInfo frame ordering: native `ChangeVPBitMap` replies `SafeMessage` and
  `DispMessage` at successive profile-owned frame boundaries on both fixed PAL
  and alternating NTSC/ECS timing; Exec reply delivery remains the scheduler
  owner.
- DBufInfo envelope alignment: mapped guest swaps require the complete public
  0x54-byte span at an even 68k address just like allocator-owned envelopes;
  an odd but byte-readable span remains unclaimed for native/provider code.
- CloseScreen copper teardown: synthetic screen closure retires compatibility
  wrappers and clears the complete public `ViewPort` copper-link quartet,
  matching `FreeVPortCopLists`; foreign screen ownership remains untouched.
- Active-view publication ordering: a status-aware `LoadView` owner observes
  the same guest `GfxBase->ActiView` pointer that it is asked to schedule;
  declined timed or untimed handoffs restore the previous pointer before the
  call is left for native/provider ownership.

- RethinkDisplay native-tail parity: the CopperStart Intuition rethink path
  refreshes owned extended-View `CurrentMonitor`/`TopLine` sidecars without
  invoking a second display publication; compact, foreign/provider, and RTG
  paths remain outside the portable claim.
- LoadView(NULL) native-tail teardown: blanking clears only the
  `CurrentMonitor`/`TopLine` values previously published by this instance,
  restores them if a status-aware owner declines, and preserves a native or
  provider replacement; rebinds relinquish claims tied to the old GfxBase.
- AmigaBoot LoadView native-tail seam: scheduler-owned activation and blanking
  use sidecar-only refresh/clear calls, including idempotent ViewExtra edits;
  the compact host image remains intentionally outside the full native-tail
  claim.
- Native overlay envelope retry: a repeated same-base ROM install rebinds the
  portable registries and retries display-database publication when Exec's
  full GfxBase MonitorList envelope appears after the gateway table; compact
  and provider-owned images remain outside the claim.
- Native-base rebind refusal: overlay publication verifies the portable core's
  actual bound base and restores a pre-transition font-list claim when the
  native sidecar transition is refused.
- RTG `LoadView` provider fallback: ROM-overlay, normal LVO, and direct host
  entry points all honor a status-aware `TryLoadView` callback. A declined
  callback preserves D0/cycles for native tail chaining; an accepted callback
  publishes the classic void-vector success, while the legacy void callback
  remains an always-claiming compatibility path.
- Direct CopperScreen/console RastPort helpers: `GraphicsServices` direct
  `Move`/`Text`/`Draw`/fill/state calls share the portable adapter; direct
  planar coverage includes guest glyph rendering, patterned lines, and
  inclusive fills, while declined layered/RTG operations retain the
  context/provider fallback. A registered layer backend is also proven to
  receive direct layered `Text`/`Draw`/`SetRast`/`RectFill` calls without a
  portable planar mutation. Direct `InitView` also shares the portable
  full-envelope clear/default-origin lifecycle boundary, and direct
  `InitVPort` now shares the guarded clear/default-priority projection
  boundary. Direct `LoadView` also shares the scheduler-aware standard-view
  publication path and preserves the provider fallback boundary. Direct
  `InitRastPort` now shares the atomic standard RastPort default-state path;
  direct `TextExtent`/`TextFit`/`FontExtent` share the portable metric boundary,
  direct `WeighTAMatch` shares the portable positive font-match boundary,
  preserving matcher failure separately from the valid zero score so malformed
  guest attributes remain available to native/provider ownership; direct/mapped
  coverage proves valid exact scores and malformed tail-chain parity, and
  direct `AskSoftStyle`/`SetSoftStyle` share the portable style boundary;
  direct `SetABPenDrMd`/`SetWriteMask`/`SetMaxPen`, the matching pen/mode
  getters, and `SetOutlinePen` share the portable RastPort state boundary;
  direct `SetRPAttrsA`/`GetRPAttrsA` now share the bounded transactional
  RastPort tag-list boundary for pens, draw mode, mask, outline pen, MaxPen,
  font, SoftStyle, and validated non-layered draw bounds; malformed lists and
  high RastPort source-field addresses are rejected before low-alias reads;
  initialization, drawing, area/flood, pattern, clear, scroll, and rollback
  paths use the same checked byte/word/long field envelope;
  provider-owned/layered state remain available to the native/provider path;
  direct `OpenFont`/`CloseFont`/`AskFont`/`AddFont`/`RemFont` plus
  `ExtendFont`/`StripFont` share the portable font lifecycle boundary;
  direct `ReadPixel`/`WritePixel`/`PolyDraw`/`DrawEllipse` plus
  `ClearEOL`/`ClearScreen`/`EraseRect`/`ScrollRaster`/`ScrollRasterBF` now
  share the portable drawing boundary;
  direct `AreaMove`/`AreaDraw`/`AreaEllipse`/`AreaEnd`/`Flood` now share the guarded
  collector and planar-fill boundary;
  direct `BltPattern` now shares the guarded stencil/area-pattern boundary;
  direct `BltTemplate` and `BltClear` now share the guarded template/memory
  blit boundary;
  direct `BltBitMap`/`ClipBlit`/`BltBitMapRastPort` now share the portable
  planar blit boundary and preserve explicit RTG/provider fallback;
  direct `Draw` now skips off-raster line samples while preserving the guest
  endpoint and line-pattern phase;
  direct `ReadPixelLine8`/`WritePixelLine8`/`ReadPixelArray8`/
  `WritePixelArray8`/`WriteChunkyPixels` share the portable planar byte-array
  conversion boundary, including signed WORD coordinate conversion and
  negative-coordinate clipping parity through direct and mapped dispatch;
  direct `AllocRaster`/`FreeRaster`/`BitMapScale`/`ScalerDiv` share the
  portable bitmap utility and allocator boundary;
  direct `AllocBitMap`/`FreeBitMap`/`GetBitMapAttr` share the guarded standard
  planar bitmap lifecycle boundary, including an optional
  `IGraphicsDisplayMemory` address-class check for native display-DMA spans,
  while RTG bitmap ownership remains explicit;
  direct `GfxNew`/`GfxFree`/`GfxAssociate`/`GfxLookUp` share the instance-owned
  extended-node registry boundary, including guest header publication,
  association replacement, teardown, and foreign-node decline behavior;
  direct `NewRegion`/`DisposeRegion` plus rectangle and region boolean
  operations share the instance-owned guest linked-region boundary, including
  classic BOOL/void D0 conventions, rectangle-node ownership, and foreign or
  malformed-region decline behavior;
  direct `GetColorMap`/`FreeColorMap` and `SetRGB4CM`/`SetRGB32CM`/
  `GetRGB4`/`GetRGB32` share the instance-owned guest ColorMap/table boundary;
  direct `LoadRGB4`/`LoadRGB32`/`SetRGB4`/`SetRGB32` share the validated
  viewport-to-ColorMap palette boundary; RGB4 provider callbacks remain
  explicit and RTG/CyberGraphX RGB32 ownership remains unclaimed for its
  patches;
  direct `AttachPalExtra`/`ObtainPen`/`ObtainBestPenA`/`ReleasePen`/
  `FindColor`/`VideoControl` share the instance-owned PaletteExtra, pen-list,
  scalar/in-place transaction, and bounded `VTAG_NEXTBUF_CM` traversal
  boundary; foreign or RTG palette state
  remains available to native/provider ownership;
  direct simple/extended sprite and GELS vectors share the instance-owned
  sprite-pool, guest image-conversion, VSprite-list, mask, animation-buffer,
  and collision-state boundaries; hardware sprite DMA and provider-backed
  DrawGList/DoCollision publication remain explicit native/provider seams;
  direct `OwnBlitter`/`DisownBlitter`/`WaitBlit`/`QBlit`/`QBSBlit` share the
  status-aware scheduler/custom-chip ownership boundary; without an attached
  owner they preserve the guest registers for native/provider takeover;
  direct `LockLayerRom`/`AttemptLockLayerRom`/`UnlockLayerRom` and
  `SyncSBitMap`/`CopySBitMap` share the explicit layers/native backend boundary;
  lock gateway completion/block results and scheduler-aware layered RastPort
  claims cross the native-safe overlay, while foreign or unclaimed layer state
  remains outside it;
  direct `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` shares the validated planar mask/minterm
  boundary, while layered RastPorts and RTG endpoints remain provider-owned;
  direct `FindDisplayInfo`/`NextDisplayInfo`/`ModeNotAvailable`/
  `GetDisplayInfoData` plus `OpenMonitor`/`CloseMonitor` share the native
  OCS/ECS display-database and resident MonitorSpec boundaries, while unknown
  ModeIDs and foreign monitor ownership remain available to native/provider
  or CyberGraphX patches;
  direct `BestModeIDA`/`CoerceMode`/`GetVPModeID` share the standard native
  mode-selection and viewport-query boundary, with malformed guest state and
  RTG bitmap/viewports declined for provider ownership;
  direct `AllocDBufInfo`/`FreeDBufInfo` and `ChangeVPBitMap` share the guarded
  DBufInfo ownership and planar viewport-bitmap swap boundary; host-facing
  swaps also require the complete bounded viewport/RasInfo envelope and zero
  `ExtendedModes`, while RTG surfaces retain the explicit provider callback;
  direct `MakeVPort`/`MrgCop`/`FreeVPortCopLists`/`FreeCprList` share the
  portable temporary `ViewPortExtra` and copper-resource lifecycle boundary,
  with RTG View/ViewPort requests retained for provider callbacks;
  direct `UCopperListInit`/`CMove`/`CWait`/`CBump`/`FreeCopList` now share the
  instance-owned user-copper allocation, instruction publication, block
  advancement, and teardown boundary; malformed or foreign lists remain
  unclaimed for native/provider ownership;
  direct `WaitTOF`/`WaitBOVP`/`VBeamPos` share the scheduler-aware cycle and
  beam-position boundary, while RTG viewport frame timing remains declined for
  provider ownership;
  direct `ScrollVPort`/`CalcIVG`/`SetChipRev` share the standard viewport
  rebuild, scan-line, and chipset-capability boundaries, with malformed or RTG
  state left available to the native/provider owner;
  direct `InitBitMap`/`InitArea`/`InitTmpRas` share the same guarded structure
  initialization boundary; `InitBitMap` snapshots only its eight-byte
  geometry/header prefix and leaves caller-owned `Planes[]` links untouched;
  direct simple/extended sprite conversion now shares the portable
  16/32/64-pixel `ExtSprite` word-width and attached-plane envelope, including
  bounded replication, transparent padding, V39-compatible attach-marker
  publication, transactional `GSTAG_ATTACHED` even/odd pair reservation, and
  rejection of overlapping second-envelope aliases before slot publication;
  hardware sprite DMA/FMODE and soft/scan-doubled scheduling remain
  native/provider-owned;
- Guest callback execution: blitter queue cleanup, GELS collision routines,
  animation callbacks, and copper/display list ownership are never invoked as
  host function pointers.

## Remaining semantic gates

`GetBitMapAttr(BMA_FLAGS)` filters the guest result to the public
`BMF_DISPLAYABLE | BMF_INTERLEAVED | BMF_STANDARD` classification bits;
allocator-only request flags are not reported. Pure and CopperStart register
coverage exercise the same value, keeping standard planar queries separate
from CyberGraphX-owned bitmap attributes.

Registered `FreeBitMap` teardown now rejects corrupted standard-planar headers,
unreadable plane spans, and inconsistent interleaved links before any allocator
call. The same malformed-object boundary is covered by pure and CopperStart
register tests, while valid instance-owned allocations retain normal release.

`BMF_INTERLEAVED` now follows the canonical row-interleaved plane layout:
`BytesPerRow` is the aggregate row stride, each plane link starts within the
first row, and later rows are addressed with that aggregate stride. Blits,
RastPort drawing, transactional snapshots, displayable-surface admission, and
`BitMapScale` share this rule. OCS ignores the flag; ECS/AGA returns NULL when
the required contiguous block is unavailable rather than publishing a
separate-plane fallback. Direct/register two-plane scaling and the full
graphics scaffold cover the later-row address and rollback boundary.

Overlapping planar `BltBitMap` calls now validate a non-null `TempA` workspace
for word alignment and one readable source row. Complete byte-envelope checks
cover shifted and cross-plane aliases, while NULL and non-overlapping paths
retain transactional host staging without probing unused scratch. Pure and
CopperStart register coverage exercise both accepted and declined workspaces.

The shared RastPort byte/word/long field boundary now rejects a zero guest base
before probing host memory. A host mapping at address zero cannot therefore
turn a NULL RastPort into a claimed compatibility object; direct and ROM-overlay
`Draw`/`Text`/`ReadPixel`/`WritePixel` regressions preserve D0 and cycles for
the native/provider path.

The transactional pen/mode setter now follows the same boundary for its
initial old-value and line-phase reads. Odd and NULL RastPorts are rejected
before any host probe, while aligned setters still publish their derived
minterms and line-state fields atomically. Direct focused coverage proves the
no-probe ownership result; layer and CyberGraphX/provider ownership remain
separate.

Non-empty `PolyDraw` point streams now apply the corresponding guest pointer
boundary: a NULL or odd point-table base is rejected before the first word
read, even when host memory exposes those bytes. Direct-core and ROM-overlay
coverage preserve D0/cycles and the pre-call cursor/bitmap; count zero still
claims the classic empty-stream no-op without dereferencing either endpoint.

The V36 pixel-array status adapters now preserve the same ownership boundary
for explicit temporary `RastPort` workspaces. The host path validates positive
geometry and the complete padded source/destination array envelope before
reading the temporary structure; odd or malformed native links decline before
claiming the vector, while invalid arrays, empty ranges, and zero-mask writes
retain their existing portable results. Direct-core coverage spans
`ReadPixelLine8`, `WritePixelLine8`, `ReadPixelArray8`, and `WritePixelArray8`,
and the ROM-overlay test confirms unchanged registers, cycles, and planar
memory on the native tail-chain path.

Connected `PolyDraw` now applies an aggregate Bresenham-work guard after the
complete guest point stream is staged but before any destination byte is
probed. A UWORD stream whose signed-WORD segments would require more than the
portable `Int32.MaxValue` host samples declines atomically, preserving the
RastPort cursor, line phase, and planar bytes; zero-mask state-only traversal
and ordinary short chains retain their existing behavior.
Direct, CopperStart register, and mapped ROM-overlay fixtures agree on the
unchanged D0/cycles and guest raster state.

`BitMapScale` now applies the same aggregate-work ownership rule to its
destination rectangle. The portable scaler requires three bounded logical
passes (sample/probe, rollback snapshot, and publication) before allocating
its DDA/sample staging. A near-maximum but individually representable UWORD
rectangle therefore declines before changing the destination extents or plane
bytes. Pure and CopperStart register coverage preserve the void-vector D0 and
cycles; the native overlay keeps caller-owned bitmap endpoints available to
the captured resident/provider owner rather than claiming the portable decline.

The V36 pixel-line/array helpers and V40 `WriteChunkyPixels` now apply the
same bounded-work rule to logical pixels plus complete padded source rows.
Representable oversized requests decline before staging or planar traversal,
while envelopes that cannot fit the guest/portable array contract retain the
classic claimed `-1` result. Direct-core, register, and mapped-overlay tests
preserve D0/cycles and keep native/provider ownership explicit.

`Flood` now applies the same aggregate-work ownership rule to its connected
region path. After the effective destination mask is known, the portable core
requires three bounded logical-cell passes (complete destination preflight,
rollback snapshot, and worst-case connected traversal) to fit within the
`Int32.MaxValue` host contract. A larger standard-planar bitmap declines before
optional `TmpRas`, seed-color, area-pattern, plane, snapshot, or mutation reads.
Pure-core, CopperStart register, and mapped ROM-overlay tests preserve the
original D0/cycles and leave the native/provider vector available.

`AreaEnd` now applies a four-pass aggregate logical-cell guard across its
decoded polygons and ellipses before managed-mask allocation, guest temporary
raster acquisition, destination probing, or fill publication. Oversized
representable shapes preserve the collector and remain available to the
native/provider owner; empty, zero-mask, inverse-JAM1, and malformed streams
retain their existing claimed-result behavior.

`BltBitMap` now applies a four-pass aggregate logical-cell guard immediately
after clipping and before overlap/TempA checks, reusable scratch growth, plane
pointer reads, or destination validation. `BltMaskBitMapRastPort` applies a
five-pass guard before its external-mask and plane probes. A full signed-WORD
rectangle can be representable in the guest layout yet exceed the portable
host-work envelope; either request declines without allocator or raster side
effects. Direct-core, CopperStart register, and native-overlay coverage
preserve the original register/cycle frame and keep provider/native ownership
explicit.

`BltTemplate` now applies a three-pass aggregate logical-cell guard after its
clipped destination rectangle is known and before template-byte reads or
reusable scratch growth. A representable maximal signed-WORD rectangle
therefore declines without source or planar probes; zero-mask, alignment,
draw-mode, and layer/provider ownership remain unchanged. Direct-core,
CopperStart register, and native-overlay fixtures preserve the caller frame.

`ScrollRaster` and `ScrollRasterBF` now apply a four-pass aggregate-cell
guard after the full-displacement no-op boundary and before source staging or
line-state reads. A representable near-maximum destination therefore declines
without reading an unmapped source plane; ordinary overlap snapshots, clipped
logical coordinates, BPen backfill, and the void-vector native tail-chain
remain unchanged. Pure-core and direct-vs-mapped ROM-overlay coverage exercise
the bounded decline.

`ClearScreen` now applies the same admission rule across its two clipped
rectangles. The portable path accounts for both probe/publication spans and
the selected-plane rollback bytes before reading the line-pattern field or
plane pointers, so individually bounded halves cannot combine into an
unbounded host transaction. Zero-mask clears retain their successful line
state, while direct and mapped native-overlay tests preserve D0/cycles and the
standard-planar/provider boundary.

`BltClear` now accounts for its probe, rollback snapshot, and publication as
three bounded byte passes before reading or staging the destination. A
guest-valid rows-mode span that would exceed that aggregate host contract
declines without allocation or memory side effects; word alignment, fill-word
composition, late-write rollback, and native/provider ownership remain as
before. Direct and mapped overlay coverage exercise the same unchanged D0 and
cycle frame.

`BltPattern` now applies the same three-pass admission to a full destination
bitmap, including selected-plane snapshot bytes, before external-stencil or
plane reads. Large but guest-valid patterned clears therefore decline without
host traversal; effective zero-mask and inverse-JAM1 no-op semantics remain
claimable, with direct and mapped overlay ownership coverage.

`Text` now accounts for the effective selected-plane count across its
background, underline, glyph-cell, bold-smear, rollback, and publication work
before destination preflight. A guest-valid multi-plane cell that would grow
an unbounded rollback journal remains available to native/provider ownership;
the zero-mask cursor path and the separate Layers/CyberGraphX boundaries are
unchanged. Pure and ROM-overlay coverage preserve the caller's D0/cycles and
the mapped native tail-chain.

`SetRast` now applies the same depth-aware admission to its full-raster probe,
rollback snapshot, and publication passes. A representable deep bitmap can
therefore decline before any plane pointer is read when the complete
transaction exceeds the portable host envelope; zero-mask and visibility-
aware provider paths retain their prior ownership semantics. Pure and mapped
overlay coverage preserve the void-vector register frame.

`ClearEOL` now accounts for its outer rollback and nested fill
preflight/snapshot/publication work across the effective selected planes
before reading destination storage. Large but guest-valid text-height clears
therefore remain available to native/provider ownership; zero-mask and line
phase behavior are unchanged, with pure and mapped overlay coverage for the
decline boundary.

`EraseRect` now accounts for its outer rollback together with delegated
`RectFill`/`BltPattern` evaluation, selected-plane probing, nested snapshot,
and publication work before minterm or plane reads. Large valid rectangles
remain available to native/provider ownership; inverted bounds, zero-mask, and
layer semantics are unchanged, with pure and mapped overlay coverage.

`DrawEllipse` now accounts for its full clipped bounding-box rollback snapshot
alongside selected-plane outline probing and publication before reading plane
storage. A representable maximum ellipse therefore remains available to
native/provider ownership instead of entering a multi-billion-cell host walk;
zero-mask and non-layered outline-bound semantics are unchanged, with pure and
mapped overlay coverage.

`InitRastPort` now treats a nonzero compatibility default font as an explicit
provider claim. If the guest `TextFont` cannot be decoded, the void vector
remains unclaimed with the caller's D0, cycles, and complete RastPort envelope
untouched, matching the existing `SetFont(NULL)` rule; successful default-font
publication and late cached-metric rollback remain covered.

`TextFit` now short-circuits an explicit `TextExtent` whose vertical bounds or
height cannot contain the selected font. It publishes the empty result before
decoding the guest string, so malformed/provider-owned glyph storage does not
steal a native no-fit call; the horizontal and alternate-box paths remain
distinct.

`FontExtent` also consumes the trailing TextFont default-glyph slot when the
guest-memory font backend exposes it. The fallback glyph therefore contributes
to the published movement and bounds; providers without that optional slot
retain their declared-range contract.
The guest-memory decoder reads the fallback by its table index, including the
full-byte-range case.

`RectFill`/`BltPattern` now conditionally decode `AreaPtSz`: a NULL
`AreaPtrn` follows the native solid-fill path without touching the pattern-size
byte, while a non-NULL pattern retains the complete signed-height validation.
The focused pure and CopperStart tests make that field-level provider/native
ownership boundary explicit.

`AreaEnd` now conditionally decodes `AreaPtSz`, preserving the native
no-pattern area-fill field boundary while retaining strict validation for
patterned fills. Focused pure and CopperStart tests cover the malformed
trailing-byte case.

`Flood` now conditionally decodes `AreaPtSz` for the same NULL-versus-pattern
boundary. Focused pure and CopperStart tests cover a no-pattern connected
region with an unavailable trailing pattern-size byte.

`FreeColorMap(NULL)` is now an explicit successful no-op at both the portable
and native-overlay boundaries. Ownership checks remain strict for every
non-null ColorMap, and the focused direct/mapped coverage verifies that no
allocator or palette state is touched.

`FreeCopList(NULL)` is now an explicit successful no-op at the copper teardown
boundary. The registry remains strict for non-null lists, and direct plus
mapped coverage verifies that NULL teardown performs no allocation release.

`FreeCprList(NULL)` is now an explicit successful no-op at the cprlist teardown
boundary. Public envelope validation and optional backend ownership remain
strict for non-null lists; direct, register, and mapped coverage verifies that
NULL teardown performs no provider callback or allocator work.

`FreeBitMap(NULL)` is now an explicit successful no-op at the standard planar
bitmap teardown boundary. Registry ownership and full envelope validation
remain strict for non-null bitmaps; direct/register and mapped overlay coverage
verifies that NULL teardown performs no allocator or RTG probe.

`GfxFree` now revalidates the guest extended-node type, subsystem, and subtype
before any association clear or allocator release. Corrupted owned nodes
remain live and tail-chain under the native overlay.

`WeighTAMatch` now accepts readable zero-height `TextAttr` metric inputs while
retaining strict malformed/odd-address fallback and separate `OpenFont`
selected-font validation. Direct, register, and mapped tests cover the exact
score and native/provider handoff.

`WeighTAMatch` now preserves the signed `WORD` width of Kickstart's shifted
size penalty. Large upward size deltas consequently retain the native wrapped
metric instead of being widened into a host integer no-match; direct,
register, and mapped coverage prove the result and D0/cycle boundary.

`FindColor`/`ObtainBestPenA` now honor the guest `ColorMap.Type` boundary used
by native `color_distance`: V1.2 maps (`Type == 0`) ignore `LowColorBits`, while
V36/V39 maps assemble full 8-bit RGB from both tables. A conflicting two-entry
palette is covered through pure, register, and ROM-overlay dispatch, including
the first-entry tie and unchanged D0/cycle frame.

The same optional-table boundary now covers `SetRGB4CM`, `SetRGB32CM`,
`LoadRGB4`, `LoadRGB32`, and `GetRGB32`: legacy maps preserve extension words
on writes and synthesize expanded high-nibble reads. Direct/register RGB
coverage and the mapped `SetRGB32CM` path prove the low table remains
unchanged.

`OpenFont` now accepts readable zero-height requests and scores them against
the resident list; only the selected `TextFont` strike remains subject to the
nonzero lifecycle envelope. Direct/register and rebound-list mapped coverage
prove the open/close ABI and malformed fallback.

`CloseFont` now removes a non-ROM resident font from a rebound guest
`TextFonts` list when its final accessor closes. Private compatibility
registrations retain their existing ownership path; malformed guest lists and
`TE0F_NOREMFONT` remain strict native/provider boundaries. Direct/register and
mapped coverage prove the list-link and ABI transition.

`FreeVPortCopLists(NULL)` now follows the native `GfxLookUp(NULL)` boundary:
portable and CopperStart paths claim a successful void no-op before probing a
guest viewport envelope, registry ownership, display callbacks, or allocator
state. Non-NULL malformed, foreign, and stale viewports remain strict.
Direct, register, and mapped-overlay coverage proves the unchanged D0/cycle
frame and callback/allocator parity
([AROS `FreeVPortCopLists`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c),
[AROS `GfxLookUp`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxlookup.c)).

`INVALID_ID` is now a portable display-query sentinel rather than a provider
decline: `FindDisplayInfo` returns NULL, `ModeNotAvailable` returns
`DI_AVAIL_NOMONITOR`, and a null-handle `GetDisplayInfoData` query returns zero
without touching its buffer. Unknown non-sentinel IDs still tail-chain to the
native monitor/CyberGraphX owner. Pure, register, and mapped-overlay parity is
covered.

`ReleasePen(-1)` is now an explicit successful no-op at the register boundary.
The portable/native-overlay path claims the all-ones pen without requiring a
ColorMap, while real releases retain strict instance ownership and palette-state
validation. Direct and mapped parity cover foreign/unmapped A0 with preserved
cycles; the focused graphics scaffold is green at 995 tests.

The optional native `GfxBase` sidecar follows the same 68000 word-address
boundary as other guest LONG envelopes. `LoadView` and full-envelope display
database publication decline a byte-readable odd discovered base before any
`ActiView` probe, and an odd native rebind cannot move the instance-owned
registries. Direct and native-overlay coverage preserves the caller frame and
the prior sidecar publication for native/provider takeover.

The outer ROM-overlay installer also rejects odd discovered library bases
before mapping vectors or replacing resident `JMP.L` bytes. This keeps the
negative-vector envelope, positive `GfxBase` image, and portable sidecar on one
68000 word-aligned ownership boundary.

The AmigaBoot lifecycle bridge also refuses odd discovered bases before its
`ActiView`/`ChipRevBits0` reads or writes. This prevents a byte-readable native
node from changing blanking, ScreenToFront, or capability publication through
the synthetic host path.

The same bridge now rejects odd guest WORD/LONG addresses while reading a
public View chain. Odd View and odd linked ViewPort envelopes remain
unclaimed before copper/display publication, while byte-only fields retain
their normal byte access semantics.

The portable line primitive also preserves connected-endpoint ownership across
line-pattern phase transitions. In `COMPLEMENT|JAM2`, a continued segment that
starts on a pattern-zero sample may write through `BPen`, but its shared vertex
is toggled back so the preceding segment remains authoritative. Preflight and
publication share the same write predicate; the focused regression covers the
planar path while exact ROM timing and layer/provider damage remain open.

The scroll primitives now keep their line-state boundary separate from pixel
selection. Real nonzero `ScrollRaster`/`ScrollRasterBF` displacements with an
effective zero mask publish `linpatcnt=15` without source staging or bitmap
writes; zero displacement retains the unchanged phase. A failed phase write
leaves the guest phase untouched.

This audit proves manifest coverage only. The execution plan remains open for
exact Kickstart error/ordering parity, native CopperSharp68k differential
execution, custom-chip timing, complete layer clipping, full display-database
parity, and final host/native cutover. Those gates are tracked in
`GRAPHICS_LIBRARY_REPLACEMENT_EXECUTION_PLAN.md` under G02--G27 and must pass
before the compatibility fallback or ROM-safe allow-list is broadened.

The fixed-cell text path now preserves the complete unsigned `tf_XSize` WORD
movement when no `CharSpace` table is present, including the negative
`FPF_REVPATH` form. Render, destination/work preflight, underline, and metric
paths share the `-65535..65535` boundary, while explicit `CharSpace` remains a
signed-WORD provider contract. The UWORD `TextExtent.te_Width` field retains
the wrapped 16-bit representation for reverse-path movement below `-32768`. A
wide-cell planar/metric regression covers the centered strike and signed
current-X publication; provider clipping and ROM timing remain later gates.

The lifecycle audit now also covers an all-hidden `ViewPort` chain at the
Intuition `RethinkDisplay` boundary. The host validates the chain without
allocating replacement CPR/DspIns state, preserving the active copper stream,
the `ActiView` sidecar, and existing guest links for a later visible rebuild.
Malformed reconstruction and copper-publication failures now return a
nonzero V39+ status; the all-hidden validated no-op returns zero.

The layered V36 pixel-line/array provider boundary now preserves the complete
UWORD coordinate/count ABI through the register adapter and Layers bridge;
high values such as `$FFFE` remain unsigned instead of being sign-extended.

The compatibility font lifecycle now preserves the reset-scoped default font
across screen teardown and reopen. Its last screen-owned accessor closes to
zero without publishing `FPF_REMOVED`; direct backend and AmigaBoot coverage
keep non-default non-ROM removal behavior unchanged.

Validation refresh (2026-08-15): the normal emulator/test project-reference
build now completes with zero warnings/errors, and the complete portable
graphics scaffold passes 1099/1099. The G04/G07 edge coverage includes the
40000-pixel fixed-cell and reverse-path metric envelope, real zero-mask scroll
phase restart, zero-displacement no-op, and malformed destination preflight.
Provider clipping, native CopperSharp68k differential execution, exact ROM
timing, and CyberGraphX remain separate gates.

### G18 `SA_BitMap` standard-planar borrowing

The synthetic Intuition screen bridge now claims a valid standard-planar
`SA_BitMap` instead of unconditionally tail-chaining it to a provider. The
caller-owned BitMap header is checked for even alignment, complete geometry,
declared plane links, readable row spans, and valid interleaved aliases before
screen state is staged. The screen RastPort and RasInfo chain borrow that
bitmap, while the embedded `Screen.BitMap` receives a compatibility header
copy. Close and rollback retire only synthetic allocations and links; they do
not free, clear, or rewrite the caller's bitmap or planes. Malformed custom
storage remains provider-owned. The direct OpenScreenTagList lifecycle tests
cover both the successful borrow and malformed decline, and the full graphics
scaffold remains green at 1192/1192. The ownership boundary follows the
[Intuition `SA_BitMap` screen contract](https://wiki.amigaos.net/wiki/Intuition_Screens#SA_BitMap).

The same boundary accepts compact `BMF_MINPLANES` headers. Their mapped
envelope ends after the declared depth's plane pointers; the synthetic Screen
receives a cleared full-size compatibility copy plus that prefix, and close
compares only the declared fields. `OpenScreenTagListBorrowsCompactMinPlanesCustomBitmap`
keeps the compact header and planes byte-for-byte unchanged through close.

Headers with valid geometry but without `BMF_STANDARD` remain provider-owned;
`OpenScreenTagListLeavesNonStandardCustomBitmapToProvider` verifies that the
synthetic path does not publish a Screen or write the caller's error word.

The G08 constructor boundary now treats `InitArea` as descriptor-only. It
validates the even, fully addressable `AreaInfo` envelope and checked vector/
flag arithmetic, then publishes the table/cursor pointers and counts without
probing caller-owned storage. Positive, zero, odd, and currently unmapped
buffers are accepted as descriptor data; `AreaMove`, `AreaDraw`, `AreaEllipse`,
and `AreaEnd` retain the complete consumer-owned capacity/readability checks.
The focused regression and the full portable/lifecycle gates remain green
after this extension.

The G08 constructor boundary also accepts the native zero-capacity
`InitTmpRas(tmpRas, NULL, 0)` form. The descriptor is validated and published
without probing a backing span. Positive, zero, odd, and unmapped backing
pointers are all descriptor data at this vector; AreaEnd, Flood, and Text
retain the consumer-owned capacity/readability checks when they use the
temporary raster. Direct and mapped void-vector coverage records the same
D0/cycle behavior while malformed storage remains native/provider owned at the
consumer boundary.

### G08 Empty AreaEnd closure

An `AreaInfo` initialized with `buffer == NULL` and `MaxCount == 0` now has a
complete empty-close path: `AreaEnd` accepts the all-null table/cursor fields
when `Count == 0`, returns success, and leaves the descriptor unchanged.
Positive-capacity and partially-null collectors remain guarded, so this
exception cannot broaden host ownership of malformed vector storage.

### G08 AreaInfo exact-end address envelope

`InitArea` now accepts an exact one-past-the-end vector/flag buffer envelope:
when the exclusive end is `2^32`, the final guest flag byte at `$FFFFFFFF` is
valid. A sparse high-address regression checks the vector and flag pointers;
positive-capacity alignment, readable-span, and over-wrap rejection remain
unchanged.

### G08 InitArea descriptor-only ownership

The portable initializer mirrors the resident [AROS `InitArea`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initarea.c)
field sequence. It snapshots the descriptor, computes representable vector/
flag addresses, and atomically publishes the six public fields without
dereferencing the caller's buffer. Direct and CopperStart register regressions
cover sparse/unmapped pointers; area consumers continue to reject unreadable
storage before mutation.

### G19 Zero-width pixel-line ownership

`GraphicsLibraryCore.ReadPixelLine8`/`WritePixelLine8` and their status-aware
register paths now claim the documented non-negative zero-width form after
the layer check. The empty request does not inspect bitmap, mask, array, or
temporary-raster storage; direct and mapped regressions verify zero D0 and
cycle preservation. Non-empty planar conversion and layered/RTG provider
handoff remain unchanged.

### G05 SetMaxPen zero-request ownership

`GraphicsRasterOperations.SetMaxPen` now returns success for `maxPen == 0`
before reading the RastPort mask byte, matching the resident implementation's
early return. NULL and odd guest addresses therefore remain field-free no-ops
through both the direct core and CopperStart register gateway; nonzero
requests retain the existing mask and alignment checks. The source basis is
the [AROS SetMaxPen implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setmaxpen.c).

### G05 SetMaxPen nonzero write-only ownership

Nonzero `SetMaxPen` now writes the derived `RastPort->Mask` without first
reading that byte. Direct and mapped read-fault coverage proves that a
writable-but-unreadable mask remains claimable, while zero, odd, and
unwritable forms retain their existing boundaries. This follows the
[AROS SetMaxPen implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setmaxpen.c).

### G15 FreeVPortCopLists link-only ownership

The portable teardown now reads/writes only the four public copper-link LONGs
in a `ViewPort`, with rollback limited to those same links. An unreadable
unrelated `DWidth`/`DHeight` field no longer prevents a valid direct or mapped
teardown from being claimed. The behavior follows the native field contract
shown by the [AROS FreeVPortCopLists implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c).

### G01 SetOutlinePen exact-field ownership

The portable setter now reads/writes only the previous outline pen and the
`Flags` word. Unreadable intervening `DrawMode`, `AreaPtSz`, or `linpatcnt`
bytes no longer prevent direct or mapped publication of the new pen and
`AREAOUTLINE` bit. The source contract follows the [AROS SetOutlinePen implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setoutlinepen.c).

### G04 SetFont exact-cache ownership

The portable SetFont path now reads/writes only the font pointer, algorithmic
style byte, and cached height/width/baseline words. `TextFlags` and `TxSpacing`
remain untouched and unread, preserving caller/native ownership even when
those bytes are sparse. Direct and mapped coverage verifies the unchanged
spacing and void-vector register frame. The source basis is the [AROS SetFont implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setfont.c).

### G05 SetAPen/SetBPen/SetDrMd/SetABPenDrMd minterm cache

The four RastPort pen/mode setters regenerate all eight private minterm bytes
from the public foreground/background/draw-mode fields. Their portable read
envelope now excludes the old minterm contents: the address span is validated
for publication, and a read-faulting but writable cache remains claimable. A
rollback image is read when available or deterministically reconstructed from
the old scalar fields. Direct and mapped tests exercise every vector with a
faulted cache and verify minterms, line phase, Flags, D0, and cycles. Source
references: [SetAPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setapen.c),
[SetBPen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setbpen.c),
[SetDrMd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setdrmd.c),
[SetABPenDrMd](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setabpendrmd.c).

### G06 Move cursor/phase write envelope

`Move` consumes the existing `Flags` word and publishes `cp_x`, `cp_y`,
`linpatcnt`, and `FRST_DOT`. The old cursor and pattern-phase bytes are not
native inputs, so the portable path address-validates those destinations and
allows write-valid/read-faulting storage. When readable, the old values remain
available for rollback after an injected late write failure. Direct and mapped
tests fault both cursor words and the phase byte and verify the new coordinates,
phase, flag, D0, and cycles. Source: [AROS Move](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/move.c).

### G06 WritePixel private-colour ownership

`WritePixel` now validates `RastPort->Flags` before probing the pen or bitmap.
When `RPF_NO_PENS` is present, the portable path declines because it has no
provider-side colour sidecar; a native/CyberGraphX owner can then supply the
private colour and perform the write. Direct and mapped read-fault coverage
verifies that `FgPen`, both destination planes, D0, and cycles remain
untouched. Source: [AROS WritePixel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/writepixel.c).

### G06 Draw/PolyDraw private-colour ownership

The connected line family now checks `RastPort->Flags` and declines
`RPF_NO_PENS` before public APen/BPen reads. This preserves native/provider
ownership of the private GC colours used by Draw and its PolyDraw loop. Direct
and mapped tests fault both public pen bytes and verify no planar mutation,
register publication, or cycle change. Sources: [AROS Draw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/draw.c),
[PolyDraw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/polydraw.c),
[private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G08 DrawEllipse private-colour ownership

DrawEllipse now declines a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` flag before probing public
`FgPen`; an unreadable optional flag does not expand the resident vector's
failure envelope. Direct and mapped read-fault tests verify unchanged ellipse
planes, D0, and cycles. Sources: [AROS DrawEllipse](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/drawellipse.c)
and [private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G03/G04 SetFont AlgoStyle ownership correction (2026-08-15)

`SetFont` now publishes the guest font pointer and cached
`TxWidth`/`TxHeight`/`TxBaseline`, clears `RastPort.AlgoStyle`, and
preserves caller-owned `TxSpacing`. The direct core, CopperStart register
gateway, and mapped ROM overlay compare the reset/metric state and restore it
on a late write failure. The reset rule follows the public
[`SetFont` autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0479.html).

### G06/G07 BltPattern zero-effective-mask admission

`BltPattern`/`RectFill` now compute the effective destination mask immediately
after the bitmap header and `RastPort.Mask` are admitted. A zero result does
not read `DrawMode`, `AreaPtrn`, stencil bytes, or public pens; the direct and
mapped regression preserves the planar bytes, D0, and cycles. Selected-plane
source, clipping, and rollback behavior remains in the portable owner, while
Layers, RTG, and CyberGraphX remain provider-owned. A readable `RPF_NO_PENS`
marker still declines to that provider/native owner before the no-op path.

### G11 BltTemplate zero-effective-mask ownership

`BltTemplate` now honors readable `RPF_NO_PENS` before admitting its zero-mask
fast path. The direct and mapped regression proves private-colour calls remain
unclaimed with unchanged D0/cycles and planar bytes, while ordinary zero-mask
templates retain the bounded no-staging behavior. Source alignment, clipping,
and selected-plane rollback remain portable; Layers, RTG, and CyberGraphX keep
their provider ownership.

### G04/G06 Zero-effective-mask admission

`Text` and `Draw` derive the effective write mask from the validated bitmap
depth before reading public pens. With no selected plane they still consume
their source/line state and publish the documented cursor transition, but
skip `FgPen`/`BgPen` reads and destination probes. Direct and mapped fault
injection coverage proves the sparse no-write envelope; nonzero masks retain
the normal pen and provider ownership boundary.

### G15/G17 ViewExtra TopLine publication

The native extended-View sidecar now includes `ViewExtra.TopLine` alongside
`ViewExtra.Monitor`. For registry-owned associations, `LoadView` publishes
the word to `GfxBase.TopLine` in the same transaction as `ActiView` and
`CurrentMonitor`; rollback and active-view fingerprinting cover all three
fields. Compact images, foreign/provider nodes, and CyberGraphX remain
outside this optional native-tail path. Layout references:
[GfxBase](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_3._guide/node0612.html)
and [graphics/view.h](https://d0.se/include/graphics/view.h).

### G15/G17 CurrentMonitor publication

`GraphicsLibraryCore.LoadView` now handles the optional native
`GfxBase.CurrentMonitor` sidecar for owned extended Views. The registry exposes
an owned `ViewExtra` lookup; the core validates `EXTEND_VSTRUCT`, the backlink,
and the monitor pointer, then journals and publishes `CurrentMonitor` beside
`ActiView`. Direct and CopperStart regressions cover monitor changes,
status-owner rollback, and the void mapped ABI; compact and foreign/provider
ViewExtra paths remain unclaimed.

### G15/G18 native display-database rebind ownership

The portable core now couples native GfxBase rebinding with the private
display-database sidecar it allocated. A different target base is accepted
only after the old owned pointer is safely detached; unreadable or uncleared
guest state leaves the previous base and ownership unchanged. Provider
replacement is relinquished without freeing provider memory. Direct coverage
proves publish/rebind/republish reuse and final release on both base fields.

### G18 native display-database sidecar initialization

The full native GfxBase bridge now clears the complete private
`DisplayInfoDataBase` sidecar allocation before publishing its magic/version,
record count, and ModeID table. Reused public memory cannot retain stale
records in the unused tail; a failure remains unclaimed and the allocation is
released before the GfxBase APTR changes. The sidecar is still separate from
the public `FindDisplayInfo`/`GetDisplayInfoData` contract and from
CyberGraphX/RTG records.

### G15/G18 ColorMap default DisplayInfo handle ownership

`ColorMap.NormalDisplayInfo` and `CoerceDisplayInfo` now validate portable
DisplayInfo handles through the display database. The zero-monitor lores
record uses its private nonzero handle, and `GetVPModeID` maps that handle back
to public ModeID zero; foreign or malformed handles remain provider-owned.

### G15/G17 ViewPort default-layout ownership

Resident field: `ViewPort.SpritePriorities` at `$22`; constructor default:
`$24`. The value is centralized as
`GraphicsLayouts.ViewPortDefaultSpritePriorities` and is consumed by both
`GraphicsRasterOperations.InitializeViewPort` and the AmigaBoot synthetic
Screen projector. This is guest-layout state and must not be independently
redeclared by a host implementation.

### G03 Metric-query versus strike ownership

The metric vectors now have a dedicated query decoder. A readable fixed-cell
TextFont can be measured with zero `tf_YSize` or without mapped strike rows,
because the resident metric paths consume scalar/table movement and bounds
fields rather than glyph pixels. Rendering and `SetFont` continue to use the
strict strike decoder. Direct and CopperStart native-overlay coverage verifies
the result envelope and register frame. Sources:
[AROS `TextLength`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textlength.c),
[AROS `TextExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/textextent.c),
[AROS `FontExtent`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/fontextent.c).

### G02 SetFont default-font ownership

The pure `SetFont` path now resolves a NULL font through
`IGraphicsFontBackend.TryGetDefaultFont`, then atomically publishes the
selected font and cached height/width/baseline. A backend without a default
font remains transparent to native/provider ownership; guest-list and mapped
register paths preserve their existing `GfxBase->DefaultFont` behavior. Source:
[AROS `SetFont`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setfont.c).

### G01/G02 SetRPAttrsA default-font delegation

The pure `RPTAG_Font=0` tag now delegates to `SetFont(NULL)` instead of
requiring the caller to provide a separately resolved default address. Mapped
calls may still pass the guest-list default as an optimization; a backend with
no default remains unclaimed. Source: [AROS `SetRPAttrsA`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setrpattrsa.c).

### G01/G02 InitRastPort guest-list default

The CopperStart `InitRastPort` adapter now prefers the rebound guest
`GfxBase->DefaultFont` when a font-list backend is installed, publishing the
same cached `TextFont` metrics as `SetFont(NULL)` before claiming the void
vector. The compatibility callback remains the host-shim fallback, and an
undecodable guest default leaves the original D0/cycles and RastPort bytes
untouched for native/provider ownership. Source: [AROS `InitRastPort`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initrastport.c).

### G01/G02 native-overlay InitRastPort ownership

When a mapped native overlay has no rebound guest font list, its
`InitRastPort` adapter now declines before invoking the host compatibility
callback. This keeps host font pointers and cached metrics out of native
RastPorts and preserves D0, cycles, and guest bytes for resident Kickstart
ownership; host-shim and rebound guest-list sessions remain claimable.

### G04/G05 soft-style scalar ownership

`AskSoftStyle`/`SetSoftStyle` now consume only the intrinsic
`TextFont.tf_Style` byte, matching the resident field sequence. A sparse font
whose metric or strike fields are unreadable can still answer and update
soft-style state, while `Text`, `TextLength`, and font selection retain their
complete validation. Direct and mapped coverage verifies the complement,
algorithmic-byte publication, D0, and cycle behavior. Sources: [AROS
AskSoftStyle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/asksoftstyle.c),
[AROS SetSoftStyle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/setsoftstyle.c).

### G02/G03 AskFont query ownership

`AskFont` now decodes only the four fields used by the resident query and
does not apply the lifecycle/rendering requirement that `tf_YSize` be
nonzero. A readable zero-height font is copied into a fully preflighted
`TextAttr`; malformed or late-faulting output remains transactional. Direct
and mapped coverage verifies the field values, D0, and cycles. Source: [AROS
AskFont](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/askfont.c).

### G09 InitBitMap descriptor-only ownership

`InitBitMap` now snapshots and publishes only the eight-byte geometry/header
prefix (`BytesPerRow`, `Rows`, `Flags`, `Depth`, and padding). It never reads
or clears the caller-owned `Planes[]` links, so a sparse or currently unmapped
plane table remains available to the native/provider owner. Bitmap readers and
display paths retain their own declared-depth plane-span and DMA checks. Source:
[AROS `InitBitMap`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/initbitmap.c).

### G08 InitTmpRas descriptor-only ownership

`InitTmpRas` now validates and snapshots only the even, fully addressable
`TmpRas` descriptor before atomically publishing `RasPtr` and `Size`. The
resident initializer does not dereference the caller-owned backing span, so a
positive, zero, odd, or currently unmapped pointer is published without
claiming the later AreaEnd/Flood/Text operation. Those consumers keep their
operation-specific capacity and readable-span checks. The focused sparse-span
regression verifies the direct and register-gateway void ABI. Source: [AROS
`InitTmpRas`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/inittmpras.c).

### G15/G18 GetVPModeID ColorMap-first ownership

`GetVPModeID` now reads `vp_ColorMap` before entering the broader viewport
assembly validator. An instance-owned map can therefore answer the mode query
without an unrelated geometry or `RasInfo` read; null-map assembly keeps the
existing full structural guard, and foreign maps remain a native/provider
boundary. Direct-core and CopperStart register coverage faults the RasInfo
link while preserving the native ModeID and cycle frame. Source: [AROS
`GetVPModeID`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/getvpmodeid.c).

### G15/G17 LoadView hidden-viewport ownership

Portable `LoadView` validation and active-view signatures now consume only
`Modes`/`Next` for `VP_HIDE` nodes. Visible ViewPorts retain the complete
RasInfo/BitMap envelope; hidden malformed or unmapped payloads remain outside
the compatibility owner’s read set. The AmigaBoot signature cache mirrors the
same field order, keeping direct, mapped, and boot publication idempotent. New
regressions cover a malformed direct/mapped payload and an unmapped boot
RasInfo field. Source: [AROS display traversal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/graphics_display.c).

### G15/G16 MrgCop hidden-viewport ownership

`MrgCop` now reads only `Modes`/`Next` for `VP_HIDE` nodes and skips their
RasInfo/display payloads. An all-hidden chain returns `MCOP_NOP` without a
copper callback; visible nodes retain strict RasInfo cardinality checks.
Direct, mapped, and AmigaBoot coverage includes a malformed hidden payload.
Source: [AROS MrgCop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/mrgcop.c).

### G07 RectFill/BltPattern private-colour ownership

The shared fill path now checks a readable `RastPort->Flags` word for
`RPF_NO_PENS` and declines before public APen/BPen probes. Because native
BltPattern does not consume that internal word, unreadable optional flags do
not reject sparse layouts; the guard only fires when the private ownership bit
is observable. Direct and mapped tests cover both vectors, public pen faults,
unchanged planes, D0, and cycles. Sources: [AROS RectFill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/rectfill.c),
[BltPattern](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/bltpattern.c),
[private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G15/G26 native-base backlink migration

During a successful native-base cutover, the portable instance rewrites the
`ExtendedNode.xln_Lib` field of every owned extended node and resident
`MonitorSpec` to the discovered `GfxBase`. The two registry batches are
transactional and restore all earlier fields on refusal; a sidecar-detach
failure also rolls both batches back. New objects use the same current base at
allocation time. This inventory item covers instance-owned guest linkage only;
monitor-list ordering, copper publication, and RTG/CyberGraphX records remain
provider-owned.

### G15/G26 Resident MonitorList cutover

Resident `MonitorSpec` nodes opened before native takeover are moved from an
exact instance-owned compatibility list into an empty native
`GfxBase.MonitorList`, including list sentinels, `ln_Succ`/`ln_Pred`, and
`ExtendedNode.xln_Lib`. An unmapped compact old list is accepted only when
owned nodes remain unlinked; readable non-empty/provider lists are refused.
The complete guest write set is transactional and restores the previous list
and backlinks on failure. Copper publication and CyberGraphX/RTG monitor
records remain outside this inventory item.

### G18 Resident MonitorSpec names

Unnamed `OpenMonitor` mode-ID requests now publish instance-owned canonical
`pal.monitor`/`ntsc.monitor` strings through `MonitorSpec.xln_Name`, reusing the
same guest address across opens. The optional post-commit write keeps native
list/refusal rollback unchanged; named opens preserve the caller pointer.
Private display-record lists, provider monitor callbacks, and CyberGraphX/RTG
families remain outside this boundary.

### G07 Clear/scroll minterm-cache ownership

`ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `EraseRect`, `ScrollRaster`, and `ScrollRasterBF`
now treat the eight-byte `RastPort.Minterms` cache as derived rollback state.
Readable cache bytes remain the exact restoration image; when a provider-backed
guest faults reads from that private span, the portable path reconstructs the
image from `FgPen`, `BgPen`, and `DrawMode`. Direct and mapped erase/scroll
coverage confirms that writable standard-planar operations remain claimable
without weakening the existing layer/provider boundary.

### G11 BltTemplate private-colour ownership

`BltTemplate` now checks a readable `RastPort.Flags` word for `RPF_NO_PENS`
after the resident DrawMode/bitmap envelope and before public pen reads. The
portable path declines provider-owned private colours without reading the
template or mutating destination planes; unreadable optional flags retain the
ordinary public-pen path. Direct and mapped tests preserve the caller frame,
D0, cycles, and planar bytes.

### G04 Text private-colour ownership

The portable Text path now checks the already-read `RastPort.Flags` word for
`RPF_NO_PENS` before public pen selection, glyph decode, or planar writes.
Private-colour ownership therefore declines cleanly to the native/provider
renderer, with direct and mapped fault-injection coverage proving unchanged
planes, D0, and cycles. Sources: [AROS Text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/text.c)
and [private GC definitions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aros-development-team/AROS/master/rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h).

### G06 PolyDraw zero-effective-mask pen ownership

The connected-line preflight now collapses the write mask against bitmap depth
before probing public pens. Zero-mask PolyDraw remains a bounded guest cursor
and line-phase operation, with private-colour and layer/provider ownership
outside the portable path; direct and mapped tests preserve D0, cycles, and
planar bytes.

### G06 WritePixel zero-effective-mask pen ownership

`WritePixel` now collapses the write mask against bitmap depth before probing
`FgPen` or inverse-video/JAM2 `BPen`. A zero-effective-mask request succeeds
without changing selected planes or claiming sparse public colour bytes, while
`RPF_NO_PENS` remains a provider/native decline. Direct and mapped coverage
preserves D0, cycles, and the planar byte fingerprint.

### G06/G08 zero-effective-mask pen admission for DrawEllipse and AreaEnd

The ellipse and recorded-area paths now collapse the declared bitmap mask
before reading public foreground/background pens. Zero-effective-mask calls
keep their successful bounded outline or collector-reset behavior, while
`RPF_NO_PENS` and layer/provider ownership remain outside the portable claim.
Direct and mapped coverage preserves raster/collector bytes, D0, and cycles.

### G08 AreaEnd/Flood private-colour ownership

`AreaEnd` and `Flood` decline a readable `RPF_NO_PENS` RastPort before
`FgPen`, `BPen`, or `OutlinePen` reads. The direct and CopperStart mapped
fault-injection tests preserve the recorded collector, destination planes,
D0, cycles, and zero faulted public-pen reads. This is a provider/native
ownership seam, not a CyberGraphX implementation; unreadable optional Flags
and layered/RTG ports remain governed by their existing boundaries.

### G07/G08 Clear, erase, and scroll private-colour ownership

`ClearEOL`, `ClearScreen`, `EraseRect`, `ScrollRaster`, and `ScrollRasterBF`
now use the shared public-pen admission seam. A readable `RPF_NO_PENS` word
declines before `BPen`/`FgPen` reads; unreadable optional Flags remains
permissive. Direct and CopperStart mapped fault-injection coverage preserves
the caller frame, cycles, and planar bytes, while layers/RTG/CyberGraphX stay
outside the portable OCS/ECS renderer.

### G15/G18 OpenWindow reconstruction rollback

The CopperStart Intuition bridge claims an `OpenWindow` only through a
successful `RethinkDisplay` handoff. A declined rebuild closes the newly
created window claim and returns NULL; existing screen and provider ownership
remain unchanged. Direct lifecycle coverage records the close callback and
the preserved failure result.

### G15/G18 OpenWindow screen-admission rollback

The Intuition bridge requires a non-NULL Screen from the compatibility handoff
before invoking `RethinkDisplay`. A NULL handoff closes the new Window claim,
skips reconstruction, and returns the documented NULL result. The direct
lifecycle regression preserves the close address and proves no empty-view
publication is attempted; foreign/provider display ownership remains outside
this inventory item.

### G15/G18 OpenScreen NULL-handoff admission

but require a non-NULL Screen before rethink or success finalization. A
permissive host/provider completion callback therefore cannot publish an empty
screen session. Direct lifecycle regressions cover the ordinary and tag-list
entry points; concrete synthetic allocation rollback remains owned by
`CompleteScreenOpen`.

lifecycle/provider ownership boundary remains explicit.
