pen bytes and verify the two-plane result without changing the guest layout.

`FloodMulticolorJam2DepositsEncodedPlanesWithoutReadingPens` and
`AreaEndMulticolorJam2DepositsEncodedPlanesWithoutReadingPens` pass; the
complete graphics scaffold is 1204/1204 and isolated builds are warning-free.
Layer clipping/damage, RTG/CyberGraphX providers, native timing, and full
profile parity remain open inventory gates.

## G09 `GetBitMapAttr` field-level ownership (2026-08-16)

The portable bitmap attribute query now isolates BMA_HEIGHT, BMA_DEPTH, and
BMA_WIDTH reads from unrelated Flags and plane-pointer storage. BMA_FLAGS
still reports only public BMF bits; a non-displayable result needs only the
Flags byte, while DISPLAYABLE is retained only after full standard-planar
capability validation. Pure and register coverage confirms the field-level
boundary without changing the guest layout or CyberGraphX handoff.

`GetBitMapAttrReadsOnlyTheRequestedScalarField` passes, and the broader
bitmap/raster lifecycle set is 37/37. The full graphics scaffold is 1205/1205,
with isolated builds warning-free; remaining profile/malformed bitmap parity
stays open inventory work.

## G14 `GetRGB4` high-table field ownership (2026-08-16)

`GetRGB4` now validates the instance-owned ColorMap and entry count, then
reads only the selected legacy `ColorTable` word. It no longer requires the
guest `ColorMap.Type` byte or the optional `LowColorBits` entry, so a sparse
extension cannot make a valid RGB4 query fall through to a provider. RGB32
and palette mutation continue to use their complete V36/V39 entry envelopes.

`GetRgb4ReadsOnlyTheRequestedColorTableWord` passes through the pure and
CopperStart register paths; the ColorMap subset is 27/27 and the complete
graphics scaffold is 1206/1206. RTG/CyberGraphX palette ownership and native
custom-chip publication remain separate inventory gates.

## G18 default screen ColorMap publication (2026-08-16)

The synthetic standard-planar screen owner now creates a `ColorMap` on every
successful `OpenScreen`/`OpenScreenTagList`, not only when palette or
`VideoControl` tags request one. The default count is `max(32, 1 << depth)`;
explicit `SA_ColorMapEntries` still wins. The ViewPort link and ColorMap
backlink are published before display reconstruction, and the map is released
only after the compatibility teardown envelope has been validated.

Close clears the owned ColorMap header before returning its Exec block, which
keeps stale Type/Count/pointer fields from contaminating a later un-cleared
allocation while preserving provider-owned replacements. The public layout
and CyberGraphX/RTG boundary are unchanged.

Validation: `OpenScreenPublishesTheDefaultColorMapForEverySyntheticViewport`
passes; the OpenScreen subset passes 111/111 and `AmigaBootMemoryTests`
passes 286/286; the complete graphics scaffold remains 1206/1206. The rule
is grounded in the classic [`OpenScreen` contract](https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/OpenScreen).
Layer damage, RTG/CyberGraphX, and native custom-chip timing remain open
inventory gates.
## G15/G16 `WaitBOVP` assembling-viewport admission (2026-08-16)

`WaitBOVP` no longer requires a non-NULL RasInfo chain merely because the
scroll validator does. The new timing-only admission checks the aligned,
mapped ViewPort envelope and standard extended-mode byte, accepts a null
RasInfo during construction, and validates any present chain before display
callback ownership. `WaitBovpAcceptsAnAssemblingViewportWithoutRasInfo`
proves direct and register parity; malformed-chain/provider and full scaffold
tests remain green. No bitmap, layer, or RTG/CyberGraphX ownership moved.

## G15/G16 `CalcIVG` display-list-only validation (2026-08-16)

The portable CalcIVG admission now consumes only the aligned View link and
`ViewPort.DspIns` field. A NULL display-list pointer remains valid for an
unmade/behind viewport; an odd pointer is declined before callback ownership.
RasInfo, bitmap geometry, and the other copper-list links stay outside this
query's portable envelope.

`CalcIvgAcceptsAnUnmadeViewportWithoutReadingRasInfoOrGeometry` and the
malformed-list regression pass through direct and CopperStart dispatch; the
full graphics scaffold is 1208/1208 and isolated builds are warning-free.
The source boundary is the classic
[CalcIVG autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/CalcIVG).

## G15/G16 `GetVPModeID` no-ColorMap field boundary (2026-08-16)

The native no-ColorMap query now validates only the aligned `vp_Modes` word,
standard `vp_ExtendedModes`, and a present `vp_RasInfo` chain. Sparse
assembling ViewPorts no longer need unrelated geometry to resolve their mode;
foreign maps, extended modes, malformed chains, and odd pointers retain the
provider/native fallback boundary.

`GetVPModeIDAcceptsASparseModeOnlyViewportThroughDirectAndCopperStart` passes
through pure and CopperStart paths; the focused filter is 12/12 and the full
portable scaffold is 1209/1209. Isolated builds are warning-free. Contract
source: [GetVPModeID autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/GetVPModeID).

## G06 `Draw` lazy pen admission (2026-08-16)

The portable line primitive now treats `FgPen` and `BPen` as source-selected
fields rather than unconditional RastPort prerequisites. It only reads
`FgPen` for a visible patterned source-one sample and only reads `BPen` for a
visible JAM2 source-zero sample; COMPLEMENT, all-zero JAM1 patterns, and
fully clipped lines remain pen-free while still committing the documented
cursor and line-pattern phase. Required late pen failures roll back the
preflighted raster and line state, and the CopperStart adapter preserves the
void-vector D0/cycle ABI on success or decline.

`DrawJam1WithNoForegroundSamplesDoesNotRequireForegroundPenAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
passes; the Draw-focused set is 25/25, the complete portable scaffold is
1210/1210, and isolated builds are warning-free.
The source contract is the classic
[`Draw` autodoc](https://amigadev.elowar.com/read/ADCD_2.1/Includes_and_Autodocs_2._guide/node0436.html).
Layer clipping/damage, CyberGraphX/RTG, and custom-chip timing remain open.

## G04/G05 `Text` lazy pen admission (2026-08-17)

Portable planar text now treats public pens as source-selected fields. It
reads `FgPen` only for a visible source-one template cell, inverse-video JAM2
background, or underline, and reads `BPen` only for a visible non-complement
JAM2 source-zero cell. All-zero JAM1 glyphs, zero-mask cursor updates, and
hidden/off-raster cells retain the native/provider boundary without probing
those bytes. ColorTextFont source-color remapping remains explicitly eager.

`Jam1TextWithAnAllZeroGlyphDoesNotRequireForegroundPenAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
passes; the text-focused set is 51/51, the full portable scaffold is 1211/1211,
and isolated builds are warning-free. Contract source:
[`Text` autodoc](https://d0.se/autodocs/graphics.library/Text).

## G04 zero-effective-mask metric-only text (2026-08-17)

`Text` now admits a zero-effective-mask request through metric glyph tables
only. The cursor still consumes the requested characters, but the portable
path does not require the strike bytes or ColorTextFont plane pointers that
would be unused by the zero write. The CopperStart adapter applies the same
zero-mask ownership check; nonzero masks retain strict strike validation.

`ZeroEffectiveMaskTextUsesMetricGlyphsWithoutReadingTheStrike` covers direct
and register dispatch with an unmapped guest strike; the complete portable
scaffold is 1212/1212. Layer clipping/damage,
CyberGraphX/RTG, and native timing remain outside this portable claim.

## G17 `ChangeVPBitMap` focused exchange admission (2026-08-17)

The portable swap path now reads the `ViewPort.RasInfo` pointer and
`vp_ExtendedModes` directly, validates the bounded RasInfo chain and current
or replacement bitmap layouts, and leaves unrelated viewport geometry outside
its ownership set. A faulted `DWidth`-through-`SpritePriorities` span does not
block a valid direct or mapped swap; nonzero extended modes, malformed chains,
foreign DBufInfo, RTG bitmaps, and incompatible layouts still decline before
the guest association or scheduler callback changes.

Evidence: `ChangeViewPortBitMapReadsOnlyTheRasInfoAndBitmapExchangeFields`
passes, the focused `ChangeVPBitMap` filter passes 14/14, and the full
graphics scaffold passes 1214/1214. Layer damage, RTG/CyberGraphX, and frame
timing remain provider-owned.

## G17 `AllocDBufInfo` focused admission (2026-08-17)

The DBufInfo allocator now validates only `ViewPort.RasInfo`, its bounded
chain, and `vp_ExtendedModes` before capability probing and allocation. A
faulted `DWidth`-through-`SpritePriorities` span does not block a valid direct
or mapped allocation; malformed chains and nonzero extended modes still
decline without allocator/provider side effects.

Evidence: `AllocDBufInfoReadsOnlyTheRasInfoAndStandardModeFields` passes, the
allocator-focused filter passes 8/8, and the complete scaffold passes
1214/1214. RTG/CyberGraphX and display timing stay provider-owned.

## G17 `ScrollVPort` focused offset admission (2026-08-17)

The portable `ScrollVPort` path now validates only the aligned viewport
RasInfo link, standard-planar extended-mode byte, and bounded RasInfo chain
before calling the display rebuild boundary. A faulted viewport geometry span
does not block a valid direct or mapped offset refresh; malformed chains,
nonstandard modes, and provider-declined status still preserve native/provider
ownership and the void-vector ABI.

Evidence: `ScrollVPortReadsOnlyTheRasInfoAndOffsetRefreshFields` passes, the
ScrollVPort-focused filter passes 11/11, and the complete scaffold passes
1215/1215. Layer damage, RTG/CyberGraphX, and custom-chip timing remain
provider-owned.

## G15/G16 `WaitBOVP` timing-field admission (2026-08-17)

The portable WaitBOVP validator now consumes only the aligned viewport
`DHeight`, `DyOffset`, standard `ExtendedModes`, and `RasInfo` fields. It
accepts a null RasInfo during viewport assembly and preserves bounded
validation for a present chain, while unrelated display/copper fields remain
available to native/provider ownership. A faulted `DWidth` no longer prevents
a valid timing wait from reaching the display boundary; the void-vector D0
and cycle state remain unchanged on the mapped path.

`WaitBovpReadsOnlyTimingFieldsBeforeItsDisplayBoundary` passes through direct
and CopperStart dispatch, the focused WaitBOVP filter passes 8/8, and the
complete scaffold passes 1216/1216. Layer damage, RTG/CyberGraphX, and exact
custom-chip timing remain explicit provider/native gates.

## G07 `ClearEOL`/`ClearScreen` zero-mask field set (2026-08-17)

The clear vectors now admit the bounded no-op after reading only the aligned
RastPort layer/provider marker, bitmap header, and normalized destination mask.
For an effective zero mask they reset `LinePtrn` and skip text-font geometry,
cursor words, public pens, draw mode, and plane storage. Nonzero masks retain
the complete text geometry and transactional planar path.

`ClearVectorsWithZeroEffectiveMaskDoNotReadPublicPensOrGeometryAcrossDirectAndMappedPaths`
faults the pen, `CurrentX`, and `CurrentY` fields and passes through direct and
mapped dispatch. The clear-focused subset passes 15/15 and the complete
portable scaffold remains 1216/1216. CyberGraphX/RTG and display/timing
ownership remain outside this portable field set.

## G12 timed blitter FIFO schedule-peek field set (2026-08-17)

The schedule-peek boundary consumes only queue state, the candidate's
`SubmittedCycle`, and (when supplied) its `BeamSynchronized`/`BeamSync` pair.
It rejects an in-flight queue, a future submission, or a false beam predicate;
with a null predicate it returns the due QBS head for the profile-aware
CopperStart owner to arbitrate. Later QBlit entries remain gated behind that
head. No guest node payload, bitmap, display, or CyberGraphX/RTG state is read
by this portable admission check.

`TimedBlitterFifoSchedulePeekHonorsDueCycleBeamPredicateAndInFlightBoundary`
covers the field set and preserves the queue's custom-chip/provider boundary.

## G24/G26 `GfxNew` extended-node publication field set (2026-08-17)

The `GfxNew` transaction owns the aligned public allocation span, its full
zero-initialized envelope, the `NodeType`/`NodeSubsystem`/`NodeSubtype` bytes,
and the shared `xln_Lib` backlink. A complete pre-publication snapshot is
restored if any clear or metadata write fails; no registry node or association
is published until every field succeeds. The operation does not inspect
provider display state, layer objects, or CyberGraphX/RTG memory.

`GfxNewRestoresExistingEnvelopeWhenMetadataPublicationFails` covers the
late-write rollback and provisional allocation release.

## G24/G25 `NewRegion` header field set (2026-08-17)

The Region allocation transaction owns only the aligned `RegionSize` public
header: its four signed bounds words and the first-rectangle pointer. The full
header is read before publication and restored on any write failure; no
rectangle nodes or provider/layer state are touched by `NewRegion`.

`NewRegionRestoresExistingHeaderWhenPublicationFails` covers this field set and
the provisional public allocation release.

## G24/G26 `GfxFree` backlink teardown field set (2026-08-17)

The teardown transaction owns the aligned association field in an instance-
owned ViewExtra/ViewPortExtra envelope and the matching registry entry. It
reads and snapshots the complete LONG before clearing; a partial/failed clear
restores all four bytes and leaves the node discoverable and allocated. Node
metadata, foreign nodes, provider display state, layer objects, and
CyberGraphX/RTG memory remain outside this portable ownership set.

`GfxFreeRestoresTheGuestBacklinkWhenItsLateClearFails` covers partial clear,
registry retention, and retry release.

## G24/G26 `GfxAssociate` backlink publication field set (2026-08-17)

The association transaction owns the aligned four-byte backlink in the new
node and, for a displaced ViewExtra/ViewPortExtra, the corresponding four-byte
backlink in the old node. Both are read and snapshotted before publication;
any partial clear restores all bytes and leaves the original registry entries
live. Node metadata, opaque monitor nodes, providers, layers, and
CyberGraphX/RTG memory remain outside this field set.

`GraphicsExtendedNodeAssociationRestoresPartialBacklinkWrites` covers both
partial-write boundaries and the successful retry handoff.

## G16 `FreeVPortCopLists` teardown field set (2026-08-17)

The teardown transaction owns only the four aligned public ViewPort copper
links (`DspIns`, `SprIns`, `ClrIns`, and `UCopIns`). It keeps LONG-read
validation, but snapshots and restores each four-byte field byte-wise so a
partial LONG clear cannot leak into the guest chain. ViewPort geometry,
RasInfo, ViewPortExtra, private CPR allocations, hardware copper state, and
CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remain outside this field set.

`FreeVPortCopListsRestoresLinksAfterAPartialLongWrite` covers the field set.

## G14 `AttachPalExtra` publication field set (2026-08-17)

The allocation transaction owns the aligned guest PaletteExtra envelope, its
WORD-sidecar spans, and the ColorMap PaletteExtra backlink. Complete byte
snapshots are restored on any late clear, semaphore/list metadata, or final
backlink failure before the three provisional allocations are freed. Existing
ColorMap state, palette registry ownership, Exec lock state, providers, and
CyberGraphX/RTG surfaces remain outside the transaction.

`AttachPalExtraRestoresAllocatedEnvelopesWhenTheFinalLinkWriteIsPartial`
covers the field set and retry release.

## G14 `GetColorMap` allocation field set (2026-08-17)

The allocation transaction owns the aligned public ColorMap header, its
ColorTable span, and its LowColorBits span. Complete byte snapshots are
captured before zeroing/link publication and restored on any late failure;
the instance registry is updated only after all fields succeed. Sparse fresh
spans may use deterministic zero snapshots; provider palette state and
CyberGraphX/RTG surfaces remain outside this portable set.

`GetColorMapRestoresAllGuestEnvelopesWhenMapPublicationFails` covers the field
set and allocator retry release.

## G14 `SyncPaletteExtra` publication field set (2026-08-17)

The portable palette transaction owns the aligned PaletteExtra header and the
WORD-sized reference-count and allocation-list sidecars used by pen sharing.
It snapshots and restores those spans around derived-head/list publication;
ColorMap ownership, embedded Exec semaphore scheduling, native resident
vectors, and CyberGraphX/RTG providers remain explicit boundaries.

`ObtainPenRestoresPaletteSidecarsAfterAPartialSyncWrite` covers the field set
and retry path.

## G22/G26 native graphics-base rebind field set (2026-08-17)

The cutover transaction owns the portable extended-node `xln_Lib` backlinks,
resident MonitorList head/tail links, monitor-node links, and library
backlinks. It snapshots and restores those aligned LONG envelopes byte-wise;
native/provider monitor lists, display timing, and CyberGraphX/RTG ownership
remain explicit boundaries.

`NativeGraphicsBaseRebindRestoresBacklinksAfterAPartialLongWrite` covers the
field set and retry handoff.

## G18/G22 `OpenMonitor` native-list field set (2026-08-17)

The resident monitor publication owns the new MonitorSpec successor and
predecessor links, the old list predecessor successor, the GfxBase list head/
tail-predecessor, and the optional default-monitor pointer. Those aligned
LONGs are snapshotted and restored byte-wise on failure; compact images,
foreign monitor lists, display timing, and CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remain
outside this field set.

`OpenMonitorRestoresNativeListAfterAPartialLongPublication` covers the field
set and retry release.

## G22/G26 native display-database sidecar field set (2026-08-17)

The sidecar allocation transaction owns the aligned public database envelope:
its header, mode-record LONGs, and any deterministic padding. It snapshots and
restores that full byte span before releasing a failed publication; the
GfxBase display-database APTR is published only by the caller after the image
is complete. Provider/native display databases and CyberGraphX/RTG records are
not claimed by this field set.

`NativeDisplayDatabaseRestoresItsGuestEnvelopeAfterPartialInitialization`
covers the field set and retry release.

## G17/G25 `ChangeVPBitMap` field set (2026-08-17)

The exchange transaction owns only the aligned four-byte
`RasInfo.BitMap` pointer after the bounded viewport/RasInfo, DBufInfo, and
compatible standard-planar bitmap validation has succeeded. It snapshots and
restores that pointer byte-wise on a failed publication; the replacement
bitmap, DBufInfo scheduler state, presentation callbacks, layers, and
CyberGraphX/RTG ownership remain outside this field set.

`ChangeVPBitMapRestoresTheOldRasInfoPointerAfterPartialLongPublication`
covers the field set and retry release.

## G15/G25 native LoadView sidecar field set (2026-08-17)

The native View transaction owns only the aligned GfxBase sidecars that this
portable instance has proved readable and writable: ActiView and optional
CurrentMonitor/TopLine fields. Probe snapshots and byte-wise rollback cover
partial publication and status decline; View/RasInfo/copper topology,
display-provider scheduling, layers, and CyberGraphX/RTG state stay outside
the field set.

`LoadViewRestoresNativeActiveViewAfterPartialCommitPublication` covers the
field set and retry release.

## G14/G25 ColorMap WORD field set (2026-08-17)

The palette update transaction owns only the selected ColorTable and optional
LowColorBits WORDs after the existing map-entry admission. It snapshots the
old values and restores both bytes of every changed WORD on failure; reserved
high nibbles, pen-sharing sidecars, display callbacks, and CyberGraphX/RTG
palette ownership remain outside this field set.

`SetRgb32CmRestoresTheLowWordAfterARejectedPartialWordWrite` covers the field
set and retry release.

## G20/G21/G25 `AddBob` field set (2026-08-17)

The Bob admission transaction owns the Bob system flags, VSprite system flags,
and VSprite-to-Bob owner LONG. It restores those aligned fields byte-wise
before list insertion is visible; GELS links, SAVEBOB buffers, collision state,
hardware sprites, and provider draw ownership remain outside this field set.

`AddBobRestoresBobFlagsAfterARejectedPartialWordPublication` covers the field
set and retry release.

## G20/G21/G25 `RemIBob` field set (2026-08-17)

The Bob teardown transaction owns the Bob system flags, VSprite owner LONG,
and the four reciprocal VSprite link LONGs touched by `RemVSprite`. It
restores all fields byte-wise after a late failure; SAVEBOB buffers, collision
state, copper projection, and foreign/provider GELS nodes remain outside this
field set.

`RemIBobRestoresLinksAfterARejectedPartialBobFlagWrite` covers the field set
and retry release.

## AddAnimOb chain journal

The AddAnimOb transaction journals AnimOb.NextOb, AnimOb.PrevOb, the existing
head's PrevOb, and the animation-key head pointer. Rollback now writes each
LONG as four independent bytes, so a failed partial link cannot leave the
chain half-published. Component timer/head fields and subsequent Bob/GELS
admission remain separate transaction stages.

`AddAnimObRestoresChainAfterARejectedPartialLongPublication` covers the field
set and retry release.

## AdvanceAnimOb frame journal

AdvanceAnimOb journals the seven public WORD fields OldX, OldY, X, Y, XVel,
YVel, and Clock. Rollback now writes each field byte-wise, preventing an
earlier successful position update from retaining a half-restored low byte
when a later frame publication fails. Component timers and Bob/VSprite state
are outside this frame journal.

`AnimateRestoresAdvanceWordsAfterARejectedRepeatedWordRollback` covers the
field set and retry release.

## UpdateComponent publication journal

The UpdateComponent journal covers the active component Timer WORD, VSprite X
and Y WORDs, and BobFlags WORD. Rollback writes all four fields byte-wise so a
late draw-state rejection restores the component's timer and coordinates
without relying on another WORD operation. Sequence links and provider draw
ownership are outside this field set.

`AnimateRestoresComponentWordsAfterARejectedRepeatedTimerRollback` covers the
field set and retry release.

## GELS reciprocal-link journal

The GELS link journal covers the reciprocal VSprite Prev/Next LONGs touched by
AddVSprite, RemVSprite, and SortGList. Rollback now writes every captured LONG
as four bytes, so an earlier successful insertion link cannot retain a stale
low byte after a later list publication fails. Sentinel fields, ordering
inputs, and provider draw/copper state remain outside this journal.

`AddVSpriteRestoresLinksAfterARejectedRepeatedLongRollback` covers the field
set and retry release.

## Collision routine publication journal

SetCollision owns one collision-table routine LONG after validating the
GelsInfo collision-handler envelope and entry index. Its rollback now writes
the captured routine bytes independently, keeping a failed entry retryable
without expanding ownership into callback execution or provider collision
dispatch.

`SetCollisionRestoresTheRoutinePointerAfterARejectedRepeatedLongRollback`
covers the field set and retry release.

## AddVSprite flags journal

The AddVSprite transaction owns the VSprite flags WORD alongside its four
reciprocal link LONGs. Rollback restores both bytes of the flags field after
link publication fails, preserving the original user/system flag envelope for
a retry; list ordering and provider draw/copper state remain separate.

`AddVSpriteRestoresFlagsAfterARejectedRepeatedWordRollback` covers the field
set and retry release.

## Static-component timer journal

The bob-less UpdateComponent transaction owns only the active AnimComp Timer
WORD. Its rollback writes both bytes independently, retaining the original
timer when the component has no Bob and the adapter rejects repeated WORD
access; component sequence and provider draw state remain outside this field.

`AnimateRestoresAStaticComponentTimerAfterARejectedRepeatedWordRollback`
covers the field set and retry release.

## SimpleSprite ChangeSprite journal

ChangeSprite owns the SimpleSprite POS/CTL image pointer LONG after validating
the sprite, viewport, and complete caller-owned image span. The pointer is
restored byte-wise on a rejected publication; image bytes and sprite-backend
callbacks remain outside this guest pointer journal.

`SimpleSpriteChangeRestoresTheImagePointerAfterARejectedRepeatedLongRollback`
covers the field set and retry release.

## Queued blitter link journal

The linked QBlit/QBSBlit transaction owns the new node's `BltNode.bn_Next`
LONG and, when present, the prior tail's `bn_Next` LONG. Both fields are
restored byte-wise on admission failure before the host FIFO changes, leaving
queue order and scheduler ownership untouched.

`PortableQueuedBlitterRestoresTheFirstNodeLinkAfterARejectedPartialLongWrite`
covers the field set and retry release.

## BitMapScale extent journal

The BitMapScale transaction owns BitScaleArgs destination width and height
WORDs plus the destination pixel snapshot. The extent rollback now writes both
captured WORDs byte-wise before replaying the pixel snapshot; planar source
sampling and provider/RTG surface ownership remain outside this journal.

`BitMapScaleRestoresExtentAfterARejectedRepeatedWordRollback` covers the field
set and retry release.

## PaletteExtra semaphore journal

The acquisition transaction owns PaletteExtra.Semaphore owner LONG and nest
count WORD. If the owner is published but the nest count cannot be committed,
the owner bytes are restored independently; task contention and provider/Exec
semaphore state remain outside the portable palette transaction.

`PaletteSemaphoreRestoresOwnerAfterARejectedNestPublicationRollback` covers
the field set and retry release.

## ViewPort copper-link journal

The screen/view handoff journal owns ViewPort DspIns, SprIns, ClrIns, and
UCopIns LONGs. A status-aware provider decline restores all four links through
independent byte writes before the portable call returns, leaving display
resource ownership and hidden viewport filtering outside the journal.

`FreeVPortCopListsRestoresLinksAfterAStatusDeclineRejectsRepeatedLongRollback`
covers the field set and retry release.

## Temporary ViewPortExtra transfer journal

GfxAssociate owns the temporary ViewPortExtra VPXF_FREE_ME WORD during an
explicit transfer. The marker is restored byte-wise if the clear or node
association fails, keeping the temporary association and allocator ownership
visible to a retry without changing the public ViewPort copper-link journal.

`GfxAssociateRestoresTemporaryFreeMeFlagAfterARejectedPartialWordWrite`
covers the field set and retry release.

## PaletteExtra semaphore release journal

Release owns the PaletteExtra owner LONG and nest-count WORD as a paired
semaphore state. Failed decrement or final owner-clear writes restore both
fields byte-wise, retaining task re-entry and provider/Exec ordering without
changing palette data ownership.

`PaletteSemaphoreRestoresOwnerAndNestAfterARejectedReleaseLong` covers the
field set and retry release.

## ExtSprite unassigned-pair publication journal

The automatic GetExtSpriteA failure path treats the first and attached
SimpleSprite number WORDs as one public state. Both unassigned sentinels are
published only as a committed pair; byte-wise rollback restores caller-owned
numbers after a partial/rejected second write, leaving the exhausted request
retryable and keeping native/provider sprite ownership outside the portable
journal.

`ExtendedSpriteGetRestoresBothUnassignedNumbersAfterARejectedPairWrite` covers
the field set and retry release.

## SimpleSprite failure-marker publication journal

The single GetSprite failure marker treats `SimpleSprite.num` as transactional
public state. Byte-wise rollback preserves the caller's original number after
a partial/rejected sentinel WORD, while a committed exhausted-pool request
continues to publish `0xFFFF` and leaves provider/native sprite ownership
outside the portable journal.

`SimpleSpriteGetRestoresTheUnassignedNumberAfterARejectedWordWrite` covers the
field set and retry release.

## Native display-database APTR publication journal

The native GfxBase sidecar APTR is a committed guest pointer: byte-wise
rollback restores `DisplayInfoDataBase` after a partial/rejected `LONG` before
the unpublished database allocation is freed. Existing provider/nonzero APTR
ownership and CopperSharp68k rebind boundaries remain outside the portable
claim.

`NativeDisplayDatabaseRestoresTheGfxBasePointerAfterPartialPublication` covers
the field set and retry release.

## ExtSprite allocation envelope publication journal

The AllocSpriteDataA conversion path now snapshots the complete public
ExtSprite envelope and generated CHIP image before clearing either span. A
failed clear, conversion write, or registry publication restores both spans
byte-wise before allocator release, so recycled guest memory is unchanged and
retryable. Display-DMA admission and native/provider ownership remain explicit
boundaries.

`ExtendedSpriteAllocationRestoresRecycledEnvelopesAfterLatePublicationFailure`
covers the field set and retry release.

## UCopperList internal-buffer publication journal

Intermediate UCopperList blocks now snapshot their complete public CopList and
instruction-buffer spans before clear/initialization. A rejected or partial
internal pointer/metadata write restores both spans byte-wise before allocator
release, preserving retryable lazy growth while leaving copper merge and
native/provider scheduling ownership explicit.

`UCopperListInitRestoresInternalBuffersAfterRejectedInitializationPointer`
covers the field set and retry release.

## UCopperList owner-publication journal

Newly initialized CopList/instruction buffers retain their pre-call snapshots
until the caller-owned `UCopList` links commit. A late owner-link rejection
restores all three guest envelopes before allocator release; registry admission
commits and discards the journal, while lazy `CBump` growth follows the same
rule.

`UCopperListInitRestoresInternalBuffersWhenOwnerPublicationFailsLate` covers
the field set and retry release.

## ExtendFont extension-envelope publication journal

Tagged font extension creation now snapshots the complete recycled extension
allocation and the font's extension/style fields. A rejected metadata,

## Palette mutation admission inventory (2026-08-17)

| Vector family | Native-overlay write boundary | Admission rule | Regression |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SetRGB4CM` / `SetRGB32CM` | One owned ColorTable entry plus optional LowColorBits entry | Require the selected entry's writable guest WORD spans | `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyPaletteMutationBeforeColorMapWrite` |
| `SetRGB4` / `SetRGB32` | ViewPort-linked owned ColorMap entry | Resolve the viewport map, then apply the same entry-span check | `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyPaletteMutationBeforeColorMapWrite` |
| `LoadRGB4` / `LoadRGB32` | Complete owned ColorMap palette storage | Require declared ColorTable and optional LowColorBits tables writable | `NativeOverlayDeclinesReadOnlyBulkPaletteMutationBeforeColorMapWrite` |

The portable transaction remains responsible for byte-level rollback after
admission; CyberGraphX/provider palettes remain outside this graphics-owned
inventory.

## G12 timed `OwnBlitter`/`WaitBlit` software ownership boundary

| Surface | Portable claim | Provider/native handoff | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OwnBlitter` | Acquire the timed software/FIFO gate without requiring BBUSY to be clear | The caller still owns the hardware-register safety point and must issue `WaitBlit` | `CopperStartBlitterSchedulerOwnBlitterAcquiresBeforePreviousBlitFinishes` |
| `WaitBlit` | Drain canonical DMA scheduling through the predicted completion boundary; decline if BBUSY remains | Native/provider owner can retain exact live-slot and wait-loop semantics | same regression and existing real-blitter callback |
| FIFO/ABI | Preserve non-nesting ownership, queued-node state, cycle result, and CopperSharp68k vector layout | CyberGraphX remains outside this replacement | focused scheduler 8/8; scaffold 1,451/1,451; graphics filter 1,472/1,472 |

The official Kickstart contract is that ownership may return before the
previous blit has finished and the owner must wait before using the registers;
the implementation therefore does not equate software ownership with BBUSY
clear. Exact native wait-loop timing, QBlit arbitration, and full
CopperSharp68k differential parity remain open.

## Native 68000 branch-range relaxation evidence (2026-08-20)

The relocatable native stream was 33,748 bytes for the `(1,4)` unit, 35,240
bytes after the `(1,5)` extension, 36,972 bytes after the `(1,6)` extension,
38,990 bytes after the `(1,7)` extension, 41,330 bytes after the `(1,8)`
extension, 43,986 bytes after the `(1,9)` extension, 47,056 bytes after the
`(1,10)` extension, 50,442 bytes after the `(1,11)` extension, and 56,536 bytes
after the `(1,12)` extension. When a generated
conditional branch to the shared offset-zero RTS would exceed the 68000
`Bcc.W` reach, `PatchBranch` emits a local RTS copy and branches to that copy;
no absolute code relocation is introduced. The `(1,9)` growth also routes the
native `TextExtent` NULL, `ReadPixel`, and `WritePixel` fallbacks through the same range-aware patch helper,
keeping the expanded relocatable stream valid without changing the shared
fallback ABI. The current stream also carries two local `BRA.W` islands around
the late `(4,1)` point sequence, so its early conditional dispatch remains
relocatable after the `(1,12)` growth without absolute addresses. The generated
`(1,12)` point emitter also forms each candidate
plane address in a data register, compares it against the original plane base,
and only then copies it to A3, because 68000 `ADD.L` to an address register
does not update the CCR. The native/scaffold runs in this ledger prove that
the fallback and all existing vectors still execute normally; the `(1,12)`
regression below confirms the enlarged stream as well. The next generated Y
cell was intentionally deferred at that checkpoint: adding it also pushed a
later `PolyDraw` internal branch beyond 68000 `Bcc.W` reach. The continuation
below adds the relay chain that reopened native ownership while keeping the
stream relocatable.

## G15/G17 native preallocated blank CPR/raw construction (2026-08-23)

`MakeVPort` now has a bounded native preallocated resource form: an even
`View`/`ViewPort`, non-NULL `vp_RasInfo` marker, LOF/SHF CPR wrappers, one
CopList, and one shared raw buffer. It emits `$FFFF/$FFFE`, publishes wrapper
starts/max-counts, and clears CopList `Next/System/Count`; allocator, display
register/DMA synthesis, split/malformed forms, and CyberGraphX remain outside
this unit. Evidence: `NativeGraphicsMakeVPortWiresPreallocatedBlankCopperResourcesOnAccurateM68000`,
focused family `65/65`, graphics scaffold `1595/1595`, signed audit
`892,152` bytes / `45,041` branches / `3,276` relays / `7` chains /
`3,276` boundaries.

## G02/G04/G05 native proportional `Text` 129..256-glyph walk (2026-08-23)

The native `Text` selector and guarded dynamic arm now cover exact counts
129..256. The body preflights a complete 256-byte source span (`0xFF00`),
uses the existing one-plane JAM1 and in-byte `CharLoc` renderer, and publishes
the cursor only after all source/table/destination cells pass. A malformed
final glyph leaves D0, `CurrentX`, and all destination bytes unchanged; count
257 and richer ownership forms retain the fallback owner.

passes 1/1; the graphics scaffold passes `1595/1595`; the signed-word audit

`3,276` relays / `7` chains / `3,276` fragment boundaries, with displacement
`-32,744..32,752`.

## G02/G04/G05 native proportional `Text` 257..512-glyph walk (2026-08-23)

The native `Text` selector and guarded dynamic arm now cover exact counts
257..512. The common entry envelope admits a complete 512-byte source span

preallocated `DspIns`/`CopList`, shared even raw stream, zero `Count`, positive
`MaxCount`, `$FFFF/$FFFE`, complete one-node standard-planar `RasInfo`/`BitMap`,
and matching bounded LOF/SHF wrappers. The check is read-only and precedes the
display callback; populated/split/odd/wrapping resources preserve the prior
active view. Zero-`DspIns` assembling and foreign provider/RTG/CyberGraphX links
remain outside the portable claim.

## G17 layered graphics continuation-frame fixture reconciliation (2026-08-24)

The layered boot fixture now records the canonical task-frame stack shape:
the reserved final-PC word occupies the caller-provided stack top, so a
resumed task's A7 is `stackTop - 4` until the normal RTS consumes that link.
The unified profile expectation is 47 installed gateways, matching the
current complete profile and its enhanced render-layer vector. This is a
fixture/evidence correction only; the host scheduler and provider ownership
boundaries remain unchanged.

Evidence: `CopperStartLayersBootTests` passes `49/49`; graphics scaffold
`1,669/1,669`; emulator/test build `0` warnings and `0` errors.
